adams_avalanche_glacier: Day 1: approach to a high camp near Mad Cat Meadow or Salt Creek. Day 2: alpine start, climb the Avalanche/White Salmon Glaciers to the summit, descend via the South Spur to camp. Day 3: hike out.
adams_northwest_ridge: Day 1: approach to high camp near Trail Divide or the Adams Glacier basin. Day 2: alpine start, climb the face to the ridge crest and summit, descend via the North Ridge. Day 3: hike out.
ca_mt_shasta_avalanche_gulch: Day 1: Bunny Flat to Helen Lake via Horse Camp and Olberman's Causeway, and set up high camp. Day 2: Alpine start from Helen Lake, climb through the Red Banks and over Misery Hill to the summit, then descend to camp, pack up and walk out to Bunny Flat. Single-day parties leave Bunny Flat in the very early hours and climb the whole route in one push.
or_hurwal_divide_traverse: Usually done as a very long single day by fast, experienced scramblers, or as a two- or three-night trip with camps at Thorp Creek Meadows and high on the Hurwal Divide. Day trips should start before first light.
or_three_sisters_traverse: Leave a car at the Pole Creek Trailhead and drive the other to the Devils Lake Trailhead. Single day: pre-dawn start up South Sister, down its Northwest Ridge, over Middle Sister south to north, then North Sister, and out to Pole Creek. Two days: camp near Camp Lake or the Hayden Glacier timberline between the peaks (overnight permit required), leaving North Sister for the second morning while the snow is firm.
wa_abernathy_peak_south_ridge: Long day trip from the trailhead (roughly 9-11 miles round trip with ~5,100-5,400 ft of gain), or an easier overnight with a camp at Scatter Lake before a lighter summit push.
wa_accidental_discharge_east_face: Day 1: drive to Downey Creek TH and hike ~12-13 mi / ~5,700 ft gain via Bachelor Creek to an Itswoot Ridge camp. Day 2: ~3 mi / ~2,500 ft further to a high camp near the Dome-Chickamin col (~8,500 ft). Day 3: reach the base of the East Face on the Blue Glacier and climb; return to high camp. Days 4-5: reverse the approach.
wa_agnes_mountain_south_ridge: Day 1: High Bridge to a Swamp Creek-area camp (~8.5 mi PCT). Day 2: cross Agnes and Spruce Creeks, climb to Upper Blue Basin camp (~5,000 ft). Day 3: move to a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass (~6,760 ft). Day 4: summit push via the south ridge and chimney crux (reported ~10.6 hr up, ~8.8 hr down); return to high camp. Day 5: hike out to High Bridge.
wa_alpine_lookout_round_mountain_trail: Single long day: trailhead to lookout is commonly done as a ~9.6-10.2 mile round trip with roughly 4-7 hours of hiking depending on pace and side-trips; some parties camp along Nason Ridge (e.g. near Rock Lake or Crescent Lake, accessed via side trails) to split it into an overnight.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_finger_of_fatwa: Day 1: Backpack to Upper Cathedral Lake. Day 2: Climb the route, descend to camp. Day 3: Hike out.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_middle_finger_b: Day 1: Backpack to Upper Cathedral Lake. Day 2: Climb the route, descend to camp. Day 3: Hike out.
Day 1: Backpack to Upper Cathedral Lake. Day 2: Climb the route (full day given 7 pitches), descend to camp. Day 3: Hike out.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_north_ridge: Day 1: Backpack to Upper Cathedral Lake/camp near Cathedral Pass. Day 2: Climb the North Ridge, descend, return to camp. Day 3: Hike out.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_pilgrimage_to_m: Day 1: Backpack to Upper Cathedral Lake. Day 2: Climb Pilgrimage to Mecca (half-day route), descend to camp; optionally tag the summit or Cathedral Peak. Day 3: Hike out.
wa_amphitheater_mountain_west_route: Day 1: Drive to trailhead, backpack in (7+ hours) to camp at Upper Cathedral Lake. Day 2: Alpine-start summit day — climb Amphitheater Mountain (and optionally Cathedral Peak), return to camp. Day 3: Hike out.
wa_argonaut_peak_northeast_couloir: Often climbed as one long day, or with a bivy on the approach; one trip report logged 15 hours car-to-car.
wa_artic_rose: Casual day trip: 0.5 hour drive, 1.25 hour approach, 1 hour climbing, 0.5 hour descent.
wa_astral_projection: Day trip: 0.5 hour drive, 1.25 hour approach, 1-1.5 hours climbing, 0.5 hour descent.
wa_astroglide: Full day outing: 0.5 hour drive from Seattle, 1.25 hour hike, 1.5-2 hours climbing, 0.5 hour descent.
wa_asymptotic: Day trip: 0.5 hour drive from Seattle, 1-1.5 hour approach hike, 1-2 hours for climb and setup, 30 minutes descent.
wa_austera_peak: Day 1: hike Cascade River Road/Eldorado Creek trail and Eldorado Glacier to East Ridge high camp (~7,600 ft), 5-6 hrs. Day 2: traverse the glacier system to Austera Peak and back (~4 hrs one-way plus summit climbing), optionally continuing to Klawatti/Primus as part of the broader Isolation/Inspiration Traverse. Day 3: descend to the trailhead.
wa_baring_mountain_east_face: A single long day from the Barclay Lake trailhead, with a strong case for splitting it across two: one trip to find the face and the base of the line, and a second to climb it. There is no established bivy site on the east side; camping at Barclay Lake on Trail 1055 is the nearest practical option.
wa_baring_mountain_northwest_ridge: Day trip. Most parties do it car to car in a long day, leaving Seattle early. There is no practical high camp on the route itself; if you want to break it up, camp at Barclay Lake (2.2 easy miles on Trail 1055) the night before and drive/walk back to the climbers' path start in the morning — though the lake is on a different approach and this adds mileage rather than saving it. Camping at the trailhead the night before is the simpler option.
wa_baring_mountain_oatmeal_man: Realistically a full car-to-car day with a very early start, or a two-day outing. Day 1: drive to the Barclay Lake trailhead the night before, hike the 2.2 miles to Barclay Lake in the evening and bivy near the lake (established sites exist; Wild Sky Wilderness rules apply). Day 2: leave camp before first light, brush-bash to the base of the north face, climb the fourteen pitches, top out, and take the northwest-ridge/base-jumper trail all the way down to the trailhead — you will not be returning to a lakeside camp, so carry everything over the top or accept a retrieval walk back in.
wa_bears_breast_mountain_infinite_beauty: Day 1: backpack in via the Waptus River Trail/PCT to a camp near the Waptus River bridge (~12 mi). Day 2: hike to the lowest point of the Mega Slab, climb the shallow-rib start and merge with Timeless Treasure's line, finish 3 pitches of 5.6+ on the summit block, and descend via Shovel Lake or the ascent line. Day 3: hike out.
wa_bears_breast_mountain_southwest_face: Day 1: Drive to the Dutch Miller Gap Trailhead and hike ~15 miles up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie to Dutch Miller Gap, then continue to a camp below the SW Face. Day 2: Climb the SW Face — ~1,000 ft of gully scrambling then the 3-pitch summit block (~6 hrs camp-to-summit) — and descend via rappels and downclimbing back to camp (~4.7 hrs). Day 3: Hike back out to the trailhead.
wa_bears_breast_mountain_timeless_treasu: Day 1: backpack in via the Waptus River Trail/PCT to a camp near the Waptus River bridge (~12 mi). Day 2: hike the old track along Shovel Creek to the slab base (roughly 4-4.5 hours from the trailhead), climb ~3,000 ft of 4th-class slab to the summit block, finish 3 pitches of 5.6+ to the top, and descend via Shovel Lake or the ascent line. Day 3: hike out.
wa_blood_sport: An hour or two, and best treated as an add-on rather than a destination. Drive from Seattle in about 45 minutes, walk in through the boulder field and alder, warm up, work the route, and go. It pairs naturally with the South Rib if you want to make a day of Guye's south side, or with the rest of the Snoqualmie Pass area sport crags.
wa_bowling_alley_aka_regular_route: Single-day outing: drive the forest roads to the NF-77 pullout, rack up and walk in (a few minutes) to the base, climb the 4-pitch route, rappel back to the base, and hike out to the car — easily done in half a day.
wa_cobbles_101: Single-day outing: drive the forest roads to the NF-77 pullout, rack up and walk in (a few minutes) to the base, climb the 5-pitch route, rappel back to the base, and hike out to the car — easily done in half a day.
wa_deep_blue: A long single day for a strong party, or a two-day outing with a bivy at the base of the tower after approaching the evening before. Multiple parties have completed the route in a day without simuling, so linking pitches is an option rather than a requirement. Given the 5.13c crux, most parties working the route treat it as a multi-visit project rather than an onsight day out.
wa_dirty_sanchez: Single long day: drive to the Tieton Road pullout, approach ~20-40 minutes via the spring trail and traverse, climb 7 roped pitches (about 5 hours of climbing for one party), then descend via rappel or the gully walk-off. Parties report roughly 8-8.5 hours car-to-car at an unhurried pace.
wa_ephemeral: A short afternoon outing: drive to the hairpin pullout, make the 15-minute scramble approach into the Ice Box, climb the route, then lower and walk back to the car.
wa_ez_way: Single long day: early/pre-dawn start from the trailhead; hike about five miles on the Boundary Trail past Badger Lake, then a short traverse off the trail to the base of Shark Rock's west face (most of the morning); climb EZ Way (one pitch plus scrambling); rappel and reverse the approach for the long hike out, aiming to be off the ridge before dark given the remoteness.
wa_glacier_view_temple: Single crag day: drive FR-4832/4934 to the parking area (~45-60 min from I-90), hike ~15-25 min to the East Face staging area, climb Glacier View Temple and other East Face sport lines, lower off each route, hike back out to the car.
wa_half_fast: Day trip with driving and approach totaling 3-4 hours round trip.
wa_iceman: A single-day cragging objective, typically combined with Route C and/or Route D at the same crag: drive to the hairpin turn on SR-20, approach via the slab/creek-bed trail, climb, then lower/rappel and retrace the approach to the car.
wa_junior_s_farm: Single long day: ~5-minute approach from the car up the boulder field to the base of Mossness Wall, climb the 8 roped pitches (5.5-5.9) plus 2 scramble sections to the upper bench of Full Montey, then rappel back down to the boulder field (partway down, the rappel route leaves the climbing line for a gully to climber's right) and walk out. Plan for 6+ hours car-to-car.
wa_lone_wolf: A half-day, single-pitch-crag-style outing: drive to the FR-9070 turnaround, hike ~20-30 minutes into Silver Basin to the base of The Obelisk, climb the 2-pitch Lone Wolf, rappel via the chain anchors, and hike back out to the car.
wa_main_peak_tepeh_towers: Day 1: approach to Eldorado high camp (~7,600 ft) via Eldorado Creek and Eldorado Glacier. Day 2: ~45 min glacier approach north/northwest to Tepeh Towers, climb the short route (~30 min), return to camp or continue on to Austera Peak. Day 3: hike out.
wa_north_face_of_the_mole: Day 1: Drive to Hook Creek Boulder parking area, hike to Edward Mesa or alpine camp (5,000+ ft elevation gain, 6-8 hours). Day 2: Approach The Mole base (40 minutes), climb North Face (3-4 hours), descend. Day 3: Descend to vehicles (2-3 hours).
wa_on_the_prowl: A short afternoon outing: drive to the hairpin pullout, make the 15-minute scramble approach into the Ice Box, climb the route, then lower and walk back to the car.
wa_particulate_matter: A short afternoon outing: drive to the hairpin pullout, make the 15-minute scramble approach into the Ice Box, climb one or more of the short bolted lines, then lower and walk back to the car — no camping or multi-day logistics required.
wa_project_crack: Single crag day: drive FR-4832/4934 to the parking area, hike ~15-25 min to the East Face staging area, walk the talus base around to the route, lead the crack, lower off, return via the same approach trail.
wa_ride_the_lightning_2: Single long day: drive to the Tieton Road pullout, approach ~15 minutes on foot, climb 6-7 pitches (roughly 5.5-6 hours climbing per one detailed TR, 9am-6:30pm total), then rappel or walk off. Total car-to-car time of about 9.5 hours has been reported.
wa_roofer_madness: Usually climbed as a short add-on before/after approaching to Roan Wall, or while based at the Martha's Place bivy, rather than as a standalone full-day objective.
wa_route_c: A single-day cragging objective, commonly linked with Route D and/or Iceman at the same crag: drive to the hairpin turn on SR-20, approach via the slab/creek-bed trail, climb, then lower off and retrace the approach to the car.
wa_route_d: A single-day cragging objective, commonly linked with Route C and/or Iceman at the same crag: drive to the hairpin turn on SR-20, approach via the slab/creek-bed trail, climb, then lower off and retrace the approach to the car.
wa_smears_jugs_and_rock_roll: Day 1: Hike from Snow Lakes Trailhead to Lake Viviane (6-8 hours with full pack). Establish camp at Viviane Campsite. Day 2: Acclimatization day; scout the route and set up top-rope if desired. Day 3: Climb Smears, Jugs, and Rock & Roll (1-2 hours of climbing). Day 4: Descent to trailhead (5-6 hours).
wa_wild_wild_west: Single-day outing: drive to the NF-77 pullout, approach directly to the wall base (short walk), climb 4 pitches (Grade II, a few hours round trip for a competent team), then rappel off the north end of the formation.
wa_big_four_mountain_dry_creek_route: A single long day from the trailhead: hike the approach trail/road to the Dry Creek basin, ascend the ledges, the main couloir and the red-slab traverse to the summit ridge, follow it to the true summit, then reverse via the south-ridge rappel and downclimb back to the basin and trailhead.
wa_big_four_mountain_spindrift_couloir: Typically climbed car-to-car or as a single long push: approach the basin below the North Face, climb the couloir in roughly 9 hours (first-ascent pace) to the summit ridge, then descend northwest via rappels/downclimbing to the Big Four-Hall Peak col and tree-anchored rappels through the bowl.
wa_big_kangaroo_going_down_under: A full alpine day: multi-hour approach, five pitches of sustained 5.9-5.11c climbing, and a roughly two-hour descent.
wa_big_kangaroo_kearney_thomas: A long alpine day: multi-hour approach, 7-8 pitches of sustained 5.9-5.11 climbing, and a roughly two-hour descent; strong parties may do it car-to-car, others bivy to split the effort.
wa_big_kangaroo_skinny_start: A long, sustained day: multi-hour approach, three hard pitches that join the Kearney-Thomas finish, and a descent that can run long if you go looking for rappel anchors.
wa_big_kangaroo_walkabout: A serious multi-day undertaking as first climbed: the FA team took three days ground-up, including a summit bivy, before descending via Beckey-Tate the next morning.
wa_big_snagtooth_west_ridge: Typically climbed as a single long day car-to-car; parties often return close to sunset given the brushy approach, loose scree, and slow travel. A 2-day/overnight option with a basin bivy is sometimes used, especially when combined with an adjacent objective (e.g., a Silver Star–Big Snagtooth traverse, reported at 12-18 hours).
wa_big_snow_mountain_east_buttress: A full climbing day: long approach via Hardscrabble Lakes followed by 10 pitches of climbing: plan for an early start and be prepared for a long descent/approach reversal.
wa_big_snow_mountain_east_ridge_hardscra: Given the roughly 25-mile round trip created by the Dingford Creek gate closure, this route is typically done as an overnight backpack with a camp at Hardscrabble Lakes; a single-day car-to-car push is possible only for very fit, fast parties, some of whom bike the road-walk sections.
wa_big_snow_mountain_north_slope_dingfor: Doable as a long car-to-car day for fit, route-finding-savvy parties (a similar NW-slope trip report logged roughly 6.7 hrs up / 4.8 hrs down, about 11.5 hrs total). Many parties instead backpack in and camp at Myrtle Lake or Big Snow Lake to split the trip over two days.
wa_black_peak_northeast_ridge: Commonly done as a 2-3 day trip: Day 1 hike in to Wing Lake camp; Day 2 climb the Northeast Ridge and descend via the South Ridge back to camp (a long day, often 12-17 hrs car-to-camp-to-car for strong parties doing it in one push from the trailhead); Day 3 hike out if camping two nights.
wa_blue_s_buttress: Single-day car-to-car outing: drive to the hairpin turnout, hike/scramble the approach to the base of the buttress (~1-1.5 hrs), climb Blue's Buttress via simul-climbing with roped pitches through the crux sections (~2-3 hrs), descend via the SE col and scree gully back to the car (~2 hrs) — typically 5-6 hours round trip.
wa_bonanza_peak_cascadian_route: Documented ascent used a full day (Aug 25) for the approach/travel day, followed by the climb itself; a multi-day trip overall including hike-out.
wa_bonanza_peak_oregonian_route: First-ascent party's push (from their high camp) took about 30 hours total including one overnight bivouac on route.
wa_booker_mountain_northeast_face: Multi-day: approach and establish camp near Park Creek/the base of the face; climb the face in a long single push; descend via the Booker-Buckner col to camp; hike out.
wa_booker_mountain_northwest_route: Typically a multi-day trip: Day 1 backpack in via Thunder Creek to a Park Creek Pass-area camp; Day 2 day-climb Booker (often combined with Buckner) via the Booker-Buckner col; Day 3+ hike out or continue a traverse.
wa_booker_mountain_south_ridge: Most commonly done as one very long day from the Cascade Pass Trailhead (reported parties starting ~2-3am and finishing ~7:30pm when combining with Buckner), or as a 2-day trip with a permitted overnight at Pelton Basin or Sahale Glacier Camp to shorten the summit day.
wa_cannon_mountain_northeast_ridge: Feasible as a very long single day done as a loop: ascend the NE Ridge from the Stuart Lake Trailhead parking area at the end of Eightmile Road, then descend via Prusik Pass, the Upper Enchantments, Aasgard Pass and Colchuck Lake back to the same trailhead -- about 15 miles with sustained class 3 scrambling and heavy bushwhacking. Best attempted only by strong, experienced parties; no car shuttle is needed.
wa_castle_in_the_sky: Day 1: Hannegan TH to an Easy Peak bivy. Day 2: Easy Ridge/Imperfect Impasse to the Perfect Pass area, approach and climb the route (long day, 12 pitches plus ~1,000 ft of scrambling). Day 3: descend and hike out (add a weather/rest day as needed).
wa_castle_peak_tatoosh_la_villa: Typically a single-day, car-to-car outing; often paired with a lap up the neighboring Southeast Face and/or a visit to Pinnacle and Plummer Peaks given the shared approach.
wa_castle_peak_tatoosh_southeast_face: A single long day from the Puget Sound area: drive to Reflection Lakes (roughly 2.5-3 hours from Seattle), scramble/climb to the summit (about 2-3 hours including the traverse and technical pitch), spend 30-60 minutes on top, and descend in 1.5-2.5 hours — a full round trip of roughly 4-6 hours car-to-car. Often combined with Pinnacle Peak and/or Plummer Peak in the same outing since the approach trail is shared.
wa_cathedral_peak_last_rites: Day 1: drive from the Puget Sound area (about 4.5 hours to Winthrop plus the Chewuch River Road) and hike in — strong parties do the full 17–20 miles to Upper Cathedral Lake in one long day with heavy packs, or split it with a camp partway up Andrews Creek / the Chewuch. Day 2: rest, scout the face from the lake and from the slopes toward Amphitheater Mountain, and fix the start. Day 3: climb Last Rites, descend the Southwest Route to camp. Day 4: hike out. Four days is the realistic minimum for this peak; five is comfortable and leaves a weather day.
wa_cathedral_peak_southwest_route: Day 1: drive and hike 17–20 miles to Upper Cathedral Lake. Day 2: climb the Southwest Route (a half-day round trip from camp) and, if you have the legs, Amphitheater Mountain's West Ridge across the basin. Day 3: hike out or add Remmel Mountain. Four days round trip from home is the realistic minimum; parties commonly build a 40–50 mile Cathedral Lakes loop out of it over 5 days.
wa_cathedral_rock_northeast_buttress: Long single day: leave the trailhead around 5-6am, at the base of the snowfield by mid-morning, seven pitches through the middle of the day, summit early-to-mid afternoon, descend the south side and hike out — expect 12-14 hours car to car. Two-day version: camp at Nosh Nosh Wahtum or near Cathedral Pass, start the climb early on day two with a light pack, and walk out that afternoon. A fast team starting around 6am can beat the afternoon heat and still have time to spare.
wa_cathedral_rock_northeast_ridge_2003_v: Long day trip: trailhead by 5am, Cathedral Pass and gear cache by 8:30am, on the route by mid-morning, six pitches through the middle of the day, summit early-to-mid afternoon, south-side descent and hike out — 12-14 hours car to car. A camp at Nosh Nosh Wahtum or Cathedral Pass on the night before converts it into a comfortable two-day trip and is the more common approach for a 5.9 alpine route this far from the road.
wa_cathedral_rock_northwest_couloir: Best done as an overnight. Day one: hike about 5 miles to Peggy's Pond (about 2,300 ft of gain) and camp. Day two: climb the northwest couloir in a half day from camp — a party leaving camp with two hours of light remaining can be on the summit before dusk and back at the pond before dark — then pack up and walk out the same day. It also works as a long single day from the car if you are fit, and pairs naturally with Mount Daniel from the same Peggy's Pond camp.
wa_cathedral_rock_southeast_face_chimney: Day trip (long): leave the trailhead by 5-6am, Cathedral Pass by 8:30-9am, on the summit by late morning, back at the car mid-to-late afternoon. Two-day version (more pleasant and the common choice): hike in and camp at Nosh Nosh Wahtum or at Cathedral Pass / Peggy's Pond on day one, climb early on day two and hike out the same afternoon. Camping is not permitted within 100 feet of lakes and streams; the Peggy's Pond basin is heavily used, so camp on durable ground and pack out everything.
wa_chair_peak_east_face: Single long day: alpine start from Alpental; ~2 hr approach to the Chair Peak basin; 3-pitch climb (several hours depending on party speed and conditions); rappel/downclimb descent back to the basin; hike out via Source Lake and the Snow Lake Trail.
wa_chair_peak_northwest_ridge: Single long day: ~2 hr approach to Thumbtack Rock/Chair basin; 6-pitch ridge climb (several hours given the runout, wandering nature of the route); descent via the south-side rap gully back to Thumbtack Rock; hike out via Source Lake.
wa_chair_peak_voie_de_chaise: Depart Alpental in the morning; 2-3 hrs approach to the East Face; climb the 8-pitch route; rappel the route (a single 60m rope) or descend the East Gully back to the basin.
wa_chair_peak_west_ridge: Depart Alpental; 2-2.5 hrs approach to the base of the 220 ft entrance couloir; 3-4 hrs of climbing to the summit; 1-2 hrs descent back to the Chair Peak basin via the south-side couloir.
wa_chalangin_peak_little_giant_pass_luah: Day 1: Little Giant Trailhead (2,600 ft) — ford Chiwawa River — over Little Giant Pass (6,409 ft) — descend into Napeequa Valley — camp near Butterfly Butte (~6,200 ft). Day 2: Traverse past the Pilz Glacier, gain the north ridge/gully, and scramble to the Chalangin summit (often combined with Luahna Peak and/or Clark Mountain in the same push); return to camp. Day 3: Hike out via Napeequa Valley and Little Giant Pass.
wa_chalangin_peak_southwest_face: Day 1: Drive to White River Trailhead (2,300 ft); hike White River Trail to the Thunder Creek drainage and bushwhack up to a high camp in Chalangin Basin (~5,100 ft). Day 2: Climb the south slope/southwest face (snow/crampon travel plus a short 4th-class cliff band) to the summit and return to camp. Day 3: Hike out via White River Trail. (Strong parties have also done the route car-to-car in a single very long day with a pre-dawn/midnight start.)
wa_chelan_butte_chelan_butte_trail: A half-day round trip on foot: most parties cover the roughly 7.5-mile round trip with 2,500 ft of gain in a morning or afternoon outing. The summit can also be reached by vehicle in well under an hour one-way when the road is dry.
wa_chianti_spire_lichen_bouquet: Two-day: Day 1, hike from SR 20 to the 6,400-6,600 ft bench or Burgundy Col (3-4 hours to the col), optionally climbing a second Wine Spires objective such as Burgundy Spire's North Face (5.8) or Paisano Pinnacle's West Ridge (5.8+). Day 2, traverse from the col to Chianti's east face, climb Lichen Bouquet, descend, regain the col and hike out. A fit party can do it car-to-car in a long day, as parties routinely do on the neighbouring Rebel Yell, but how little is known about this line argues for the extra time.
wa_chianti_spire_north_face: Most parties treat this as a two-day trip. Day 1: hike from the SR 20 pullout to the 6,400-6,600 ft bench (good camping, water) or push on to one of the two or three bivy sites at Burgundy Col (year-round snow for water, austere and exposed); 3-4 hours to the col. Day 2: traverse from the col to the Burgundy-Chianti notch, climb the North Face to the summit, reverse to the col and hike out. Fit parties climb Chianti car-to-car in a long day, and the North Face pairs naturally with a second Wine Spires objective - Burgundy Spire's North Face (5.8) or Paisano Pinnacle's West Ridge (5.8+) - from the same camp.
wa_chimney_peak_the_chimney: Typically three days minimum. Day 1: drive in (allow about an hour for the last 20 miles, via the North Shore detour while South Shore Road stays closed at mile 8) and hike the 13.9 miles up the East Fork Quinault to a permitted camp in or near Enchanted Valley, ~2,000 ft. Day 2: leave camp very early, work off-trail around to the southwest side, scramble the Southwest Ridge to the peak's upper terrain, climb The Chimney, and return to camp. Day 3: hike out. Strong parties sometimes split the approach differently, but East Fork Quinault River is a quota zone so your camp is fixed by whatever the permit gives you.
wa_clean_break: Most parties climb it car-to-car in a single long day from a bivy or camp near Silver Star Creek: pre-dawn approach (2.5-3.5 hr), the 15-pitch climb, and a walk-off descent, with total car-to-car times of roughly 12-13 hours reported. Some parties instead backpack in the evening before and camp in the Silver Star Creek valley to shorten the summit day.
wa_colchuck_peak_holsten_hilden: Typically climbed car-to-car in a single long winter day: approach via Colchuck Lake and the glacier basin (skis/snowshoes likely needed given the seasonal road closure), climb the AI3/M6 line to the summit ridge, then descend the standard East Route down the Colchuck Glacier.
wa_colchuck_peak_north_buttress_couloir: Usually climbed from a car camp near the trailhead or a permitted backcountry camp at Colchuck Lake, with an early alpine start to climb the couloir on firm snow before it softens and before any summit cornice becomes more hazardous to breach.
wa_crater_mountain_standard_route: Day trip: pre-dawn start from Canyon Creek TH, ~4-5 hrs up Jackita Ridge Trail to Crater Lake basin, scramble the SE ridge and crux gully to the summit, then reverse the entire route — commonly completed as one very long single day. Alternatively, backpack in and camp at Crater Lake (permit required) to split the ~15-mile round trip and ~6,300 ft of gain over two days.
wa_cutthroat_peak_cauthorn_wilson_couloi: A shoulder-season alpine ice day: early start to catch the couloir before solar warming increases avalanche/rockfall risk, roughly 7 pitches of climbing, then a ridgeline rappel descent (or summit + West Ridge descent).
wa_dark_peak_dark_glacier_route: Commonly done as a 3-day trip: Day 1 -- ferry/floatplane to Stehekin, shuttle to High Bridge, hike in to Fivemile Camp or Swamp Creek Camp (or toward Hemlock Camp on the alternate approach). Day 2 -- long, strenuous summit day: cross-country travel and bushwhacking/scrambling to Dark Fin Col, roped travel across the Dark Glacier, belayed moat crossing, short scramble to the summit, then reverse the entire route back to high camp. Day 3 -- hike out to High Bridge and catch the return shuttle/ferry to Chelan.
wa_davis_peak_nc_north_face:
Two days, one bivouac. Day 1: sleep near Diablo (camping is not allowed at the townsite; the legal option is a permitted backcountry site or a night in the Newhalem campground). Leave at first light, hike the Stetattle Creek trail about 2 mi / 3 km, drop 200 ft to ford the creek opposite Davis, then bushwhack and scramble the 3rd/4th-class rib — roping up for the slabby sections — through a slide-alder band above the cliffs to a bivouac on flat snow at the toe of the glacier, 4,000 ft. Expect to reach it by late afternoon, roughly eight or nine hours from the road; there is running water at the site. Spend the evening looking at the face and deciding whether the couloir will go.

Day 2: up the glacier at first light, gear up at the bergschrund, climb the lower band, the snowfield, the crux pitches and the upper couloir to the summit ridge near 6,700 ft. Tag the summit if you have time. Then commit to the full south-side descent — 6,000 ft — aiming to be below the cliff bands before dark, and walk or shuttle the four road miles back to Diablo.
wa_davis_peak_nc_south_slope_and_ridge: Feasible in one very long day or, more comfortably, as an overnight. Day trip: leave the Gorge Creek bridge before dawn; the South Davis saddle at 5,700 ft is about 4.4 hours from the car and the summit about 8.3 hours; allow 4.1 hours down, for roughly 13.5 hours car to car and 10 miles travelled with about 7,400 ft gained and lost if you take the Gorge Creek/South Buttress line with its detours. The round-trip figure for the direct line is 6.2 miles. Overnight: one party camped at the 5,720+ ft saddle, where there was room for two tents on a snow ledge; what is there when the snow has melted is not documented. That splits the trip into a long brushy climb on day one and a short summit push plus the full descent on day two, and it is the version to choose if you are unsure of the slab above the saddle. An overnight requires a wilderness permit.
wa_direct_north_buttress: Days 1-2: over Hannegan Pass and down the Chilliwack River Trail to camp near Brush Creek (the Bear Creek camp is closed), then ford Bear Creek and climb past Ruta Lake to the saddle camp (~6,480 ft). Days 3-4: climb the 21-pitch buttress (historically done in about 2.5 days with a bivy), then descend to camp. Days 5-6: hike back out over Hannegan Pass, about 21 miles.
wa_dome_peak_indian_summer: Typical plan: 2 days to approach to a high camp via the western (Ptarmigan Traverse/Spire Point) trail, 1 day to climb the route, 1 day to hike out — roughly a 4-day round trip. The eastern approach via Chelan extends this to about a 5-6 day trip.
wa_dorado_needle_east_ridge: Day 1: Hike from the Cascade River Road trailhead, cross a creek, and climb steeply via the Eldorado Glacier to the East Ridge of Eldorado Peak for camp setup and gear/technical review (~7,400 ft camp). Day 2: Traverse the Inspiration Glacier to the McAllister Glacier, descend to the base of the East Ridge, climb to the summit of Dorado Needle, and descend the Northwest Ridge back to high camp. Day 3: Descend to the trailhead, including the final creek crossing, typically finishing by early evening.
wa_dragontail_peak_backbone_ridge: Camp at Colchuck Lake or day-push from the trailhead; alpine start to be climbing by first light. Parties consider an ~18-hour car-to-car day civilized for the grade — move efficiently to locate the descent before dark.
wa_dragontail_peak_east_ridge_aasgard_pa: Single push: Trailhead (3,400 ft) → Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft, ~4.3 mi) → Aasgard Pass (7,841 ft) → east-ridge saddle (~8,500 ft) → summit (8,840 ft, ~6.25 mi one-way); round trip is roughly 12.5 mi, with car-to-car times reported in the 11-15 hour range depending on pace and conditions.
wa_dragontail_peak_serpentine_arete: Day 1: Drive to Stuart Lake TH (or backpack in with an Enchantments overnight permit), hike to Colchuck Lake, camp on the south shore. Day 2: Alpine start (2-4am), approach to route base (~3 hrs), climb the route (7-10 hrs), descend to Colchuck Lake and hike out (~13-14 hrs car-to-car total is typical for a fit party going car-to-car in a single push).
wa_early_winter_couloir: Typical single-day itinerary: pre-dawn start from the car, ~1 hr approach to the couloir base, 5-7 hrs of technical climbing to the col and summit, then descend via the West Couloir/Chockstone bolted rappels (not back down the couloir) in 2-3 hrs, aiming to be off all technical terrain well before dark.
wa_east_face: Day 1: Downey Creek Trailhead to Bachelor Flats camp (6 miles, 3,100 ft gain). Day 2: Bachelor Flats to Dome-Chickamin Col base camp (3.2 miles, 2,600 ft gain). Day 3: Climb East Face of Middle Gunsight (4-6 hours climbing time, 600 ft gain) and descend to base camp (3-4 hours). Day 4: Return to Bachelor Flats (5-6 hours). Day 5: Return to trailhead (6 miles, 4,500 ft loss).
wa_east_face_2: Day 1: Early departure from trailhead at Milepost 166 (~6am). Hike to bench camp at 6,500 feet (2-4 hours). Establish camp, rest, hydrate, prepare for next day. Day 2: Early alpine start from camp toward Chablis Spire via Burgundy Col or direct approach (1.5-2 hours to base). 4-pitch climb and summit (3-4 hours). Descent via 2 rappels (1-1.5 hours). Return to camp. Day 3: Pack out, return to trailhead via hiking trail (2-4 hours downhill).
wa_east_face_3: Typically done as a single long day from a car camp or bivy near Washington Pass: early start, a 45-minute-to-1-hour approach, roughly 6 pitches of technical climbing, then a 3-rappel descent back to the approach talus and the same trail out. No bivy on the route itself is standard.
wa_east_ridge_8: Full alpine day: trailhead to Castle-Pinnacle col (~2-3 hr), roped climbing to the summit (~2 hr for the three pitches), summit break, then descent (~3 hr) — commonly a 7-8 hour car-to-car day, longer if combined with The Castle.
wa_east_twin_needle_north_buttress: Day 1: Lower Goodell Creek TH to a col near the Chopping Block (~6+ mi, ~6,000 ft gain). Day 2: traverse Crescent Creek Basin, cross to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, rappel onto the Mustard Glacier, then climb the North Buttress (9 pitches, 5.9, ~2,000 ft).
wa_east_wilmans_spire: Car-to-car is feasible in a long day for a fit, fast party (biking the Monte Cristo road saves significant time and energy), but many parties break the roughly 4,000 ft of total elevation gain into an overnight at Glacier Basin, climbing East Wilmans Spire the following morning and hiking/biking back out to Barlow Pass the same day.
wa_easy_getaway: Plan a long car-to-car day: pre-dawn start, 1-2 hr approach/bushwhack to base, roughly 6-8 hrs for the 8 pitches, then 1-2 hrs to descend. Budget a full daylight window given the approach and loose descent.
wa_eldorado_peak_north_ridge: Day 1: Approach to high camp. Day 2: Descend to the North Ridge base, climb the ridge (roughly a half-day, ~5 hrs round trip from camp), descend, hike out or camp a third night.
wa_eldorado_peak_west_arete: Day 1: Approach via Eldorado Creek/Roush Creek/Eldorado Glacier to a high camp near the East Ridge base (~7,400 ft). Day 2: Continue via Dorado Col to the base of the west face and climb the ~19-pitch, ~2,800-3,000 ft arête (5.6-5.8) to the summit, then descend via the East Ridge back to camp — a long day, historically up to ~17 hours round-trip from camp. Day 3: Hike out to the trailhead.
wa_elephant_butte_standard_route: As a dedicated objective: Day 1 — drive to Diablo, hike the Sourdough Mountain Trail and ridge to a camp near Sourdough/Stetattle Ridge; Day 2 — continue the ridge traverse to Elephant Butte's summit and return. A fit, light party can also do the full round trip from Diablo in one very long day. As an approach leg into the Southern Pickets, most parties budget two to three days from Diablo to reach Elephant Butte with full overnight packs before continuing into the range.
wa_ellation: A single long day: hike in (~1 hr), climb the 8 pitches, rappel the route back to the base (8 raps), then hike out. Not typically climbed as a multi-day or bivy objective.
wa_ellen_pea: Single long day from the car: roughly 1–1.2 hour approach, 7 pitches of climbing, then rappel the route with two ropes to the base and descend the gully to the car.
wa_enchantment_enchainment: Most parties take two or three days, and the Enchantment overnight permit decides how. Without a lottery permit nobody may camp inside the permit zone (Stuart Lake, Colchuck Lake, the Core and the rest of the zone), so an unpermitted party must either do the whole loop in a single push or split it into separate day trips from the Stuart Lake trailhead, for example Stuart, Sherpa and Argonaut on one day, then Colchuck, Dragontail, Little Annapurna, McClellan, Enchantment Peak and Cannon on another. With an overnight permit, a common split is Stuart, Sherpa and Argonaut on day one with a camp in the permitted zone (Colchuck Lake or the Core), then the Colchuck-Dragontail col and the Core summits over the next one or two days before exiting.
wa_enchantment_peak_east_ridge: Commonly combined with Prusik Peak, Little Annapurna, and/or McClellan Peak in a single long day or overnight from a basin camp, since all stage from the same Prusik Pass/core basin area.
wa_fantasy_falls: Realistically a long single push in winter, or a two-day trip if you want to climb the ice with a rested party. Single push: leave the plowed Longmire-Paradise road near Narada Falls very early (2-4 a.m.), ski or snowshoe the ~3 miles of gated Stevens Canyon Road to the Bench Lake/Snow Lake trailhead, continue past Bench Lake to Snow Lake and up Unicorn Creek into the cirque, and be racking up at the base of the face around first light — figure roughly four hours car to base. Climb the three pitches to the summit, rappel the summit block and descend the south slope to the 6,605 ft col, then reverse the basin, gully and trail to the road, and ski the road back out. Two-day version: camp at Snow Lake (two designated wilderness sites, bear pole and toilet, wilderness permit required) or bivy higher in the cirque, climb the route the following morning with a short approach, and walk out the same day.
wa_first_amendment: Early start given the length (9 pitches, ~900 ft) and remote approach; expect a full, long alpine day combining the shared approach, traverse to the base, the technical pitches, and a Spontaneity-Arête-style descent.
wa_flight_of_the_falcon: Given the 6+ hour approach, parties typically either commit to a single very-early (pre-dawn) push (one reported round trip was about 17 hours 50 minutes car-to-car), or hike in during the afternoon/evening and bivy at Martha's Place boulder near the head of the basin, climbing the route the next day and hiking out — splitting the long round trip across two days.
wa_flora_mountain_southwest_slope: Day 1: Ferry/floatplane from Chelan to Stehekin Landing, NPS shuttle to Harlequin Bridge, then hike the Stehekin River Trail (~3 mi) and Devore Creek Trail (~4 mi, steep then brushy) to Bird Creek Camp (4,200 ft). Day 2: Round-trip summit push from Bird Creek Camp via the saddle south of Enigma Peak, Castle Creek crossing, and southwest ridge talus to the 8,323-ft summit and back (typically 6+ hours). Day 3: Hike out to Stehekin and catch the return ferry/shuttle. Many parties extend the trip to combine Flora with Devore and/or Tupshin Peaks from the same camp.
wa_forbidden_peak_east_ledges: Used as the descent leg after climbing the West Ridge, East Ridge Direct, or North Ridge; not typically a stand-alone objective.
wa_fortress_mountain_east_ridge: Typically a 2-3 day trip: hike in via the Chiwawa River/Buck Creek Trail to camp at the ~7,200 ft Chiwawa-Fortress col (or a 7,100 ft meadow plateau below Fortress), climb Fortress and often Chiwawa Mountain from camp, then hike back out. A car-to-car speed-traverse of both peaks (25+ miles, off-trail) has been done in just over 9 hours by a strong trail runner.
wa_fortress_mountain_southwest_face: Most parties make this a 2-3 day backpack: Day 1, hike in ~9-9.5 miles to camp at Buck Creek Pass or the alpine basin below Pass No Pass; Day 2, climb Fortress (very often combined with Buck Mountain and/or Chiwawa Mountain) from camp; Day 3, hike out. Fast parties have done it car-to-car in a single long day, with reported times ranging from under 12 hours up to about 19 hours when combined with other summits.
wa_fortune_peak_east_slope: Often combined with North or South Ingalls Peak: Esmeralda Trailhead to Ingalls Pass, into Headlight Basin (sometimes camping there), up the east slope to the Fortune Peak summit, then reverse or continue to an adjacent peak before returning.
wa_fortune_peak_standard_route: Typically a single long day: drive to the Esmeralda Trailhead, hike up the Esmeralda Basin Trail to the Ingalls Way junction, continue to the pass above Lake Ann, scramble the ridge to the summit, then reverse the entire route. Many parties combine it with South Ingalls Peak.
wa_garfield_mountain_infinite_bliss: A long single day is the norm: leave Seattle before dawn, be climbing by mid-morning, on the topout by mid-afternoon, back at the base by early evening. One documented fast ascent climbed the route in 5.5 hours (about 15 min/pitch, heavily simulclimbed), rappelled in 2.5 hours, and was back in Seattle by 9:30 p.m.; a typical strong party takes ~7 hours up and 3 hours down plus the approach.
wa_garfield_mountain_leaning_spire_west_: One very long day, car to car, with a pre-dawn start; the shared South Route approach alone takes four to five hours to reach the Y, and a Main Peak round trip on the same terrain is rarely under twelve hours. A bivy at the Glade Saddle above the slab (room for two) turns it into a comfortable two-day trip and is the traditional option.
wa_garfield_mountain_preiss_route: A very long single day or a comfortable two-day trip. The large ledge under the steeper headwall, roughly two-thirds of the way up, is described as a great bivy site and is the natural split if you want to climb the headwall pitches fresh in the morning.
wa_garfield_mountain_south_route: Twelve hours is Beckey's stated absolute minimum and a fit, competent party should plan 15-17 hours car to car: one documented ascent left the car at 6:45 a.m., summited at 2:45 p.m., started down at 3:30 p.m. and reached the car at 11:05 p.m. The alternative is a two-day trip using the two-person bivy site at the Glade Saddle above the slab.
wa_garfield_mountain_southwest_ledges: Realistically a single enormous day: leave the car by first light, expect the better part of the day for the 2,600 ft of ledge navigation, and be on the summit early enough to start rappelling Infinite Bliss with hours of daylight in hand. Some parties bivy — ascents here generally need a bivouac or one of the longest days of summer.
wa_gato_negro: Most parties base out of the bench camp (~6,500 ft) below the spire. Plan for: an early approach from camp to the base of the route, a full day on the 12 pitches (one fast party of four completed camp-to-camp, including the climb, in 9.5 hours), then the slow, loose descent gully (budget several hours). An alpine start is strongly recommended so the descent isn't finished in the dark.
wa_gilbert_peak_conrad_glacier: Plan on two or more days car to car, given the extra distance of crossing both glaciers.
wa_gilbert_peak_meade_glacier: Typically done as an overnight/2-day backpack: Day 1, hike in to a camp at Surprise Lake (wooded, sheltered) or Warm Lake (above treeline, exposed to wind); Day 2, alpine start for the summit push across the basin and up the Meade Glacier snowfields, then return to camp and hike out (or split the hike-out over a 3rd day). Strong parties have done it car-to-car in a long single day.
wa_gilbert_peak_west_route: Commonly done as a multi-summit traverse from a camp below Snowgrass Flats: Day 1, hike in to Lower Snowgrass or the timber sites below the flat; Day 2, traverse to and climb Old Snowy Mountain, Ives Peak, and Gilbert Peak in a single long day (reported round-trip totals of ~22 miles and ~7,500 ft cumulative gain/loss for the full multi-peak traverse) before returning to camp; Day 3, hike out.
wa_golden_horn_southwest_route: Day 1: Drive to the Rainy Pass trailhead, hike ~10–11 miles via the PCT over Cutthroat and Granite Passes to Snowy Lakes, make camp. Day 2: Alpine start from camp, scramble scree/talus to the summit ridge, negotiate the short 5th-class summit block, rappel/downclimb, return to camp, then hike out. Strong parties sometimes complete the whole outing car-to-car in one long day.
wa_greenwood_mountain_west_ridge: Most parties treat this as a 2-3 day trip: Day 1, hike in roughly 5 miles from the Phelps Creek Trailhead to a camp in upper Phelps Basin (~5,700-5,800 ft); Day 2, climb Dumbell and/or Greenwood via the connecting col and ledge (round trips from camp have taken roughly 8-11 hours) and return to camp; Day 3, hike out. Some strong parties have done both summits car-to-car in a single very long day (one recorded example: ~18 miles round trip with about 5,800 ft of cumulative gain, ~10 hours 45 minutes, covering both Dumbell and Greenwood).
wa_gunnshy_peak_standard_route: Single-day round trip from the Barclay Lake Trailhead: drive to trailhead, hike the spur road and climber's path via Barclay Creek crossing and the forested headwall, cross the waterfall gully, work along the ridge past the Tailgunner/Wing saddle and Point 5,760+ (via Gunn Lake basin in summer/fall or the open-slope bypass in winter/spring), scramble the summit block, then retrace the entire route back to the trailhead.
wa_gunrunner: Day 1: Downey Creek Trailhead to Bachelor Flats camp (6 miles, 3,100 ft gain). Day 2: Bachelor Flats to Dome-Chickamin Col base camp (3.2 miles, 2,600 ft gain). Day 3: Climb Gunrunner traverse of four peaks (6-8 hours climbing time, 1,500 ft gain). Day 4: Descend to base camp, then return to Bachelor Flats (5-6 hours). Day 5: Return to trailhead (6 miles, 4,500 ft loss).
wa_guye_peak_improbable_traverse: Single-day car-to-car outing from Seattle. Leave the city by 4:30-5:00 am, park at Alpental, be scrambling the talus cone by first light, aim to be starting the roped climbing within an hour of leaving the car. Expect roughly 4-5 hours on the face, then 1.5-2 hours over the three summits and down the Cave Ridge trail. Published trip reports range from about 8 hours for a fast, competent pair to 14+ hours for a party that pitches everything out - one well-known report started at 10:30 am and exited at 1 am. There is no reason to camp; if you want a relaxed day, camp at a Snoqualmie Pass area campground the night before rather than on the mountain.
wa_guye_peak_southeast_gully: A short winter day. From the PCT North trailhead, hike about 1.4 miles up the old Commonwealth Basin trail until the peak is directly west-northwest, then break uphill to the base of the gully. Climb 1,400 ft of snow that steepens from 45 to about 70 degrees, top out on the ridge between the true and false summits, and walk off east down Commonwealth or west over Cave Ridge. Start before dawn so the gully is still frozen: the sun-exposed half of the route softens quickly and the entire line becomes a wet-slide problem once it warms. There is nothing here that justifies an overnight.
wa_hadley_peak_cougar_divide: Commonly done car-to-car in a single day given the shorter, higher-starting approach: an early start, roughly 5-6 hours to the summit and back given the ~10.6-mile round trip and ~3,600 ft of cumulative gain.
wa_hadley_peak_skyline_divide: Typically done as a long single-day car-to-camp-free outing (when the trailhead is reachable): early trailhead start, roughly 4–5 hours to the summit along the ridge, and a similar time back down; some parties break it into an overnight with a ridge-camp on Chowder Ridge given the length (~14–15 miles round trip).
wa_helmet_butte_standard_route: Day 1: Drive to Trinity Trailhead (FR 6200 has been closed beyond Atkinson Flat by storm damage - verify before departure) and backpack the ~8.8-mile approach to a camp at Pass No Pass or Buck Creek Pass, both of which have multiple established sites. Day 2: Day-scramble Helmet Butte from camp (1-2 hours round trip from Pass No Pass); many parties combine the outing with nearby Fortress Mountain or Liberty Cap given the shared approach. Break camp and hike partway or fully out. Day 2 or 3: Finish hiking out to the trailhead.
wa_honeymoon_route: As with the standard route, most parties camp in Royal Basin and climb the couloir as a day mission from camp; at least one recorded ascent was completed as part of a long winter day trip.
wa_hourglass_gully_winter: Day 1: Drive from Puget Sound region (1-2 hours) to Lake Serene trailhead. Hike Lake Serene trail (2-3 hours to lake). Camp at Lake Serene if doing this as a two-day climb. Day 2: Early pre-dawn start (2:30 AM typical) from trailhead or 4:30 AM from lake camp. Approach saddle (2-3 hours), climb Hourglass Gully (2-3 hours), traverse East Ridge (1-2 hours), reach summit by mid-morning (8-10 hours from car). Descend via rappels and gully (2-3 hours). Return to Lake Serene (2-3 hours). Hike out (2-3 hours), reaching car by dark. Total single-day push: 15+ hours; two-day with camp: more manageable timing.
wa_hozomeen_mountain_north_peak_north_ro: Best done as a single very long day from Hozomeen: leave the ranger station in the dark, allow roughly 7 hours to the summit and 6 hours back for about 13 hours of moving time plus breaks. Parties who prefer not to commit to a 15-hour day can bivy on the north ridge near the 5,900-6,800 ft benches, but there is no reliable water up there, so a camp means hauling everything you will drink.
wa_hozomeen_mountain_northeast_buttress: Day 1: drive Silver-Skagit Road from Hope in the morning, start hiking mid-morning, and cover the 10.5 miles and roughly 4,000 ft of trail to the Monument 74 area camp near 6,345 ft in about 7 hours — top off water at the last forest creeks before the ridge. Day 2: leave camp at first light, drop to the 5,800 ft saddle, climb the cirque snowfields and northeast ridge to the summit, return to camp, pack, and hike out. Strong parties do the second day as summit plus full walk-out; most find it a comfortable two-and-a-half-day trip.
wa_hozomeen_mountain_west_face: Day 1: drive in from Hope, hike 11-plus miles with wall loads to a camp just north of the peak. Day 2: 4.5 hours of gully downclimbing and rib traversing to the base, then climb as far as light allows - the first ascent reached the top of pitch 10 and bivouacked. Day 3: finish the last two pitches and the 100 ft summit ridge stroll, descend the north side to camp. Day 4: hike out. A very fast, very experienced party might compress this to three days; nobody should plan on two.
wa_huckleberry_mountain_east_ridge: Typically a 2-3 day trip: Day 1 hike in to a Ridge Lake or Gravel Lake camp; Day 2 climb to the summit and descend back to camp; Day 3 hike out. A round trip of roughly 20+ miles and ~5,800+ ft of cumulative gain overall.
wa_huckleberry_mountain_south_face: Most parties treat this as a 2-3 day trip, camping at Ridge Lake or Gravel Lake, given the long shared PCT approach with the peak's other routes.
wa_icy_peak_ruth_icy_traverse: Commonly done in a long single day or as an overnight with camp near Ruth Mountain's summit or the Ruth-Icy Saddle: Hannegan Trailhead to Hannegan Pass (~4 mi), up and over Ruth Mountain, across to and up Icy Peak's Southeast summit, then reverse the entire route — a documented outing totaled about 16 miles and roughly 8,000 ft of cumulative elevation gain/loss round trip.
wa_indian_head_peak_southwest_slopes: Typically done as a 2-day (3-day for a more relaxed pace) backpack: Day 1 hike the North Fork Sauk Trail from the trailhead to a camp near White Pass or Indian Pass (roughly 10 miles to White Pass, 13-14 to Indian Pass, ~4,000+ ft gain); Day 2 climb Indian Head Peak round-trip from camp (off-trail scramble, several hours) and either hike out or camp again; optional Day 3 hike out. A very strong party can do it as a single very long day trip from the trailhead (~27 miles round trip, ~6,000 ft gain).
wa_inner_constance_northwest_buttress: Day 1: drive to the Upper Dungeness Trailhead and hike ~9.3 miles to Home Lake; if you still have daylight, push up into the Home Creek basin and camp at the boulders northwest of the summit so you can study the face in evening light. Day 2: climb the buttress, descend, and return to camp. Day 3: hike out to the trailhead. Strong parties sometimes compress this to two days by carrying to the boulder camp on day 1, but the approach mileage plus a 1,200-foot loose buttress makes three days the sane plan.
wa_inner_constance_seans_route: Single-push day from a Home Lake camp: climb the buttress (~3 technical pitches plus scrambling to the false summit), then descend via Avalanche Canyon back to Home Lake — roughly 12.5 hours round trip per the first-ascent party's report.
wa_inspiration_traverse: Day 1: Hike and scramble from the Eldorado Creek trailhead up the boulder field and basins, climb the Eldorado Glacier and camp on rock at the edge of the Inspiration Glacier; climb Eldorado in the evening if time and conditions allow. Day 2: Cross the Inspiration Glacier east, climb Austera and Primus via the Klawatti and North Klawatti glaciers, and climb Klawatti from the col camp on its south side. Day 3: Climb Dorado Needle from the McAllister Glacier side, then return over the Inspiration and Eldorado glaciers and descend to the car. Many parties add a fourth day, or split the peaks differently, especially when snow is soft or the moats are open.
wa_j_tnar: Day 1: Hike Lake Serene trail (4.1 miles, 2000 ft gain, 2-2.5 hours), approach cirque (30 min), scout wall and bivy location (1-2 hours). Day 2-5: Climbing days with portaledge camps. First ascensionists climbed Pitches 1-3 with bivy on Pitch 3. Pitch 4 (crux A3+) and Pitch 8 (Fang Roof) are highlights. Days 6-7: Finish upper pitches to summit, then full rappel descent (10-12 hours). Multiday success requires disciplined pacing and weather monitoring.
wa_jack_mountain_east_ridge: Budget three to four days, the norm on this peak. Day 1: approach and establish a camp on the eastern side of the mountain. Day 2: the climb — the published account records 9.5 hours from low on the glacier for the Skoogs' variation, so plan a pre-dawn start and a full day up and down. Day 3: return. Hold a fourth day for weather; the ridge is exposed and there is nowhere quick to go if a front arrives.
wa_jack_mountain_nohokomeen_headwall: Three days is the normal plan and is what most parties use; strong teams do it in two. Day 1: trailhead to May Creek (8 miles of easy trail, roughly 3-3.5 hours), then 3 miles of steep bushwhack to a camp at ~5,200 ft below the glacier, or push on to a glacier camp near 7,400 ft (a 6 a.m. start has reached a 7,400 ft glacier camp by 5 p.m.). Day 2: leave camp around 4-4:30 a.m., cross the glacier, climb the headwall and the summit ridge (summit typically 7:45-8:45 a.m. from a high camp, or roughly 4-5 hours from a 5,200 ft camp), then downclimb and return. Day 3: descend the bushwhack and hike out the East Bank Trail. One documented two-day trip covered camp-to-summit-and-back in an 18-hour push from the low camp.
wa_jack_mountain_north_ridge: Three to four days, in line with published notes that most parties on Jack take that long. Day 1: East Bank Trail and the off-trail climb to a camp below the ridge. Day 2: the ridge to the summit and a descent of the East Ridge back to camp - a full day. Day 3: descend the bushwhack and hike out the East Bank Trail. Hold a fourth day for weather, and note that using the Ross Lake water taxi can meaningfully shorten days 1 and 3.
wa_jack_mountain_northeast_glacier: Most parties on Jack Mountain take three to four days for any route, and there is no reason to think this one is faster. Plan on a day to cross the pass between Crater Mountain's summits and the Jerry Glacier to a camp near 6,000 ft on the east side of Jack, a full summit day on the glacier and the upper mountain, and a day to return — with a fourth day held as weather and route-finding buffer.
wa_jack_mountain_southeast_ridge_direct: Plan three to four days. Day 1: trailhead to Crater Lake, then cross-country over the Crater Mountain saddle and Jerry Glacier to a Jerry Lakes or Crater Creek camp (about 8-8.5 hours with packs). Day 2: alpine start, gain the 7,000 ft ridge step and climb the crest to the summit, descend the South Face, and return to camp — budget a full day, longer than the standard route's ~8 hours round trip from camp, because the ridge is roped terrain. Day 3: recross the glacier and saddle and hike out. A fourth day is a sensible weather buffer, and most parties on Jack take three to four days for any route.
wa_jack_mountain_southwest_ridge: Three days is realistic. Day 1: trailhead to Little Jack (6.0 mi, ~4,800 ft of gain from the junction) and on along the ridge toward the notch, camping high on the crest. Day 2: traverse to Jack's base, climb the southwest ridge to the summit and reverse it back to camp - a full day. Day 3: reverse the ridge to Little Jack and descend to the car. Most parties on Jack Mountain take three to four days by any route, and the Little Jack line is no exception despite being the shortest approach.
wa_klawatti_peak_north_ridge: Day 1: Drive to the Eldorado trailhead and hike to camp in Eldorado Basin or on the Eldorado snow dome. Day 2: Cross the glaciers to Klawatti Col and the Klawatti-Austera Col, scramble the north ridge to the summit, and return to camp or continue toward Austera Peak. Day 3: Descend to the trailhead.
wa_klawatti_peak_sw_buttress: Typically climbed as a quick add-on from an established Klawatti/icecap camp (see the Southeast Face route's 3-day traverse itinerary): approach and camp on Day 1-2, then climb the SW Buttress in 1-2 hours on a summit day alongside or instead of the south face.
wa_kyes_peak_northeast_ridge: Long single push from the North Fork Sauk trailhead, or split over two days with a camp near Curry Gap or on the ridge. Mike Heath's 1968 first-ascent account describes the outing from the road's end as taking about 4-5 hours, though this reflects a fast/direct climb rather than a typical modern car-to-car day given the approach length.
wa_le_conte_mountain_northern_aspect: Typical 2-3 day plan: Day 1 — drive to Cascade Pass Trailhead, hike to Cascade Pass and over Cache Col/Cache Glacier, descend to Kool-Aid Lake, cross Middle Cascade Glacier to Yang Yang Lakes camp (a long day, ~9,000+ ft cumulative gain over ~13 miles). Day 2 — climb Le Conte Mountain round-trip from camp via the east-slope/ledge route. Day 3 — reverse the approach back to the trailhead.
wa_lemah_two_goatshead_spire: Realistically a three-day trip. Day 1: drive to Pete Lake trailhead and hike 7-8 miles of easy trail to the PCT campsite by Lemah Creek at about 3,200 ft, or camp at Pete Lake. Day 2: leave camp before first light, follow the climbers' path and snow finger into the east-side cirque, climb the spire, and return to camp. Day 3: hike out. A fit party has done the neighbouring standard route car-to-car in 11 hours 26 minutes, but that is a snow scramble with a known line; an obscure rock tower with no known line deserves the extra day.
wa_lichtenberg_mountain_southeast_ridge: Summer: a single easy day, about 7 miles round trip with about 2,100 ft of gain. Brisbine's party made an overnight of it in September, camping at Lichtenwasser Lake and taking in both the true summit and The Lichtenhorn the following day — a pleasant way to do it if you want an unhurried trip. Winter: a full but moderate day tour, about 5.2 to 8 miles and 2,100 to 2,700 ft of gain from US 2, with the road approach taking a good chunk of the time. Start early in winter to have the road walk behind you before the snow softens and to keep your options open on stability.
wa_lichtenberg_mountain_west_face: A single day from the Smithbrook trailhead is what the original report implies: roughly an hour in, climb, walk off, and out. Camping at Lake Valhalla — dispersed sites set back from the shore, campfires prohibited — puts you directly under the wall and would suit a party wanting time to scope the line before committing.
wa_lichtenberg_mountain_west_face_west_r: Single day, car to car. Drive from Seattle (roughly 2 to 2.5 hours to the Smithbrook Trailhead via US 2) or from Leavenworth (about 45 minutes), start early, reach the PCT saddle above Lake Valhalla in about 2 hours, climb the west face and rib in 1 to 1.5 hours, and descend the Northeast Slope past Lichtenwasser Lake to the road in around 2.5 hours — roughly 6 to 7 hours total. If you would rather make it an overnight, camp at Lake Valhalla (dispersed sites, set well back from the shore, campfires prohibited) and climb the face the following morning with a light pack; this also positions you for The Lichtenhorn in good early light, which is when the west face is in the sun.
wa_little_big_chief_mountain_northeast_f: Usually a 2-3 day trip and often combined with a neighbouring peak (Summit Chief or Overcoat) from a backcountry camp near Dutch Miller Gap or Summit Chief Lake: approach and camp on day 1, climb the northeast ridge/face and return to camp on day 2, hike out on day 3. Strong parties climb it as a long day from a camp already at the gap.
wa_little_sister_north_face: Best done from a camp in the upper Green Creek basin. Day 1: drive in (allow extra time if FR 38 is gated or washed out at MP 7), cross the Middle Fork on the log, hike the Elbow Lake Trail and the Green Creek climbers' path, and camp below the Green Creek Glacier. Day 2: early start onto the glacier, climb steep snow to the base, cross the moat, climb the four pitches of the North Face, then descend either by rappelling the lookers-right side or by downclimbing the Southeast Ridge; break camp and walk out. Strong parties go car-to-car in a long day. The most efficient use of the approach is to combine routes — North Face up and Southeast Ridge down, or vice versa — or to take in Cinderella Peak across the col. The full Green Creek Circuit that includes this summit is 5.6, Grade IV, about 25 pitches over 13 miles with roughly 7,000 ft of gain, taking 10-14 hours for the traverse portion.
wa_little_sister_south_couloir: A long single day from the Elbow Lake Trailhead: a winter party left about 7 a.m., reached the summit around 1 p.m. and was back after dark, about 12 hours and roughly 10 miles and 5,000 ft car to car. The line has also been skied as part of a multi-day traverse of the whole range.
wa_little_sister_southeast_ridge: Best as an overnight. Day 1: drive to the Elbow Lake Trailhead (allow extra time if FR 38 is gated or washed out at MP 7), cross the Middle Fork on the log, hike the Elbow Lake Trail and Green Creek climbers' path, and camp in the upper Green Creek basin below the glacier. Day 2: early start onto the Green Creek Glacier, cross the moat at the Cinderella-Little Sister col, climb the three pitches of the Southeast Ridge and the fourth-class finish to the summit, then either downclimb the ridge or rappel the North Face to the glacier, break camp and walk out. Fit parties do it car-to-car in a long day; combining it with the North Face (up one, down the other) or continuing to Cinderella Peak makes far better use of the approach. The full Green Creek Circuit, which takes in this ridge, is Grade IV 5.6, roughly 25 pitches and 13 miles with about 7,000 ft of gain, and takes 10-14 hours for the traverse alone.
wa_little_sister_west_face: Realistically a two-day trip, or one very long day for a fast, fit party willing to move together. Day 1: drive in (allow extra time if FR 38 is gated or washed out), cross the Middle Fork on the log, hike the Elbow Lake Trail and Green Creek climbers' path to camp in the upper Green Creek basin below the glacier at around 4,500-5,000 ft. Day 2: cross the divide early, climb the 1,000 ft west face soloing or simul-climbing the fourth and low fifth class, tag the summit, reverse the westernmost rib to the second lower notch, regain the glacier, break camp and walk out. Parties doing the full Green Creek Circuit — a 5.6, Grade IV, roughly 25-pitch, 13-mile linkup with about 7,000 ft of gain, first done by Darin Berdinka in 2013 — take 10-14 hours for the traverse portion alone and typically go car-to-car in 12+ hours.
wa_luahna_peak_southwest_slope_southeast: 3-day itinerary as documented: Day 1 — White River Trailhead to a Boulder Creek ford camp (~3,700 ft); Day 2 (AM) — Boulder Creek camp up to a high camp in upper Boulder Basin; Day 2 (PM) — high camp to the Luahna summit via Clark Basin and Luahna Basin, then back to high camp; Day 3 — high camp back out to the trailhead.
wa_lundin_peak_east_ridge: Single-day car-to-car climb: drive to the PCT trailhead, hike the long approach over Red Pass to the Lundin/East Lundin saddle, climb the short final pitch to the summit, then rappel or downclimb back to the saddle and hike out.
wa_lundin_peak_south_face_left: Single-day car-to-car climb: drive to the Commonwealth Basin/PCT North trailhead, hike into the basin below the south face, climb the route (4 pitches), then descend via the West Ridge or Southeast Ridge and hike out.
wa_magic_mountain_north_face: Two days minimum. Day 1: drive in, hike 4.9 miles to Pelton Basin Camp (1,800 ft of gain), set camp, scout the couloir and glacier entry from the basin in evening light. Day 2: pre-dawn start, climb the couloir and Yawning Glacier to the Magic–Pelton Col, cross the head of the glacier, climb the 600 ft north face to the notch and the summit, then either reverse the glacier or descend the South Ridge and loop back over Cache Col to Cascade Pass. A three-day version lets you carry over to Kool-Aid Lake and climb another Ptarmigan Traverse peak, which is a better use of the permit.
wa_magic_mountain_northeast_couloir: Two days. Day 1: drive in, hike 4.9 miles over Cascade Pass to Pelton Basin Camp, set up, and look at the couloir in evening light to pick your line and identify the overhead hazard. Day 2: very early start, up the couloir approach and the Yawning Glacier to the Magic–Pelton Col, climb the couloir to the summit, and descend either the couloir (early, while frozen) or the South Ridge. Spring ski parties commonly link it into the Magic S Loop, an 18-mile, 9,700 ft day from the Eldorado parking area when the road is gated, which has been done in about 12 hours.
wa_magic_mountain_northwest_ridge: Two days from a Kool-Aid Lake camp is the sensible plan. Day 1: drive, 3.7 miles to Cascade Pass, over the Cache Glacier and Cache Col, drop to Kool-Aid Lake and camp (5.9 miles, ~5 hours). Day 2: cross to the base of the northwest ridge, climb it and the northwest face to the summit, descend the South Ridge back to camp, pack up and hike out over Cache Col. Parties on the full Ptarmigan Traverse can slot this in as a half-day objective from the Kool-Aid Lake camp in place of the more common South Ridge scramble.
wa_magic_mountain_southwest_cirque: Two days. Day 1: drive in, hike 3.7 miles to Cascade Pass, cross the Cache Glacier to Cache Col, descend 600 ft and camp at Kool-Aid Lake (5.9 miles, ~5 hours). Day 2: climb into the southwest cirque, take a gully to the summit ridge and the top (2-3 hours), descend the South Ridge to camp, then pack and exit over Cache Col. As with the South Ridge, this is most naturally done as a side objective from the first camp on the Ptarmigan Traverse; a car-to-car day is about 19 miles round trip.
wa_magic_mountain_west_ridge: Two days from a Kool-Aid Lake camp. Day 1: drive in, hike 3.7 miles to Cascade Pass, cross the Cache Glacier to Cache Col, drop 600 ft and camp at Kool-Aid Lake (5.9 miles, ~5 hours). Day 2: cross to the pocket glacier below the west face early while the snow is firm, cross the schrund, climb the route in four pitches or so, scramble to the summit, descend the South Ridge to camp, then pack out over Cache Col. Three days is more comfortable and lets you add the South Ridge or the Southwest Cirque as a second day's objective from the same camp.
wa_mcmillan_spire_west_southwest_ridge: Typically a 2-3 day trip: Day 1 approach to Terror Basin camp (6-8 hrs); Day 2 climb the Southwest Ridge and return to camp; Day 3 hike out via Goodell Creek.
wa_mount_adams_south_climb: Most parties do it in 2 days: hike in and camp near Lunch Counter (~9,000-9,400 ft) day one, alpine-start for the summit push, then descend to the car day two. Strong parties climb it car-to-car in a single long day (roughly 10-14 hours total).
wa_mount_baker_boulder_park_cleaver: Day 1: Hike Boulder Ridge Trail and climb to high camp (~5,700 ft). Day 2: Cross the lower Boulder Glacier northwest to the cleaver, climb it, and summit (10,781 ft), then descend to camp and out.
wa_mount_berge_east_ridge: Typically a long day or overnight from a basin camp: Day 1 - hike in to treeline via the Buck Creek Trail (~6 miles) and camp near the Cleator-Berge area; Day 2 - climb the East Ridge (roughly 6 hours of climbing, much of it simul-climbed) and descend the same way; Day 3 - hike out if camping overnight.
wa_mount_bigelow_tribute_to_richard: Best done as an overnight from Upper Eagle Lake, which is what the first-ascent party did. Day 1: drive in and hike the 6.2 miles of Eagle Lakes Trail #431 to Upper Eagle Lake (roughly 2 h 45 min of walking at the mapped trail estimate), make camp among the established sites, and spend the last of the light scoping the East Face from the lakeshore and picking your line — the crack systems are much easier to sort out with binoculars from the water than from the base. Day 2: leave camp at first light, scramble the 900–1,000 ft of talus and heather to the base, rack up, and climb the four pitches. Budget generously — the FA party's climbing was very slow because of the cleaning required, and even on a cleaned-up line this is not a fast route. Walk north to the summit, descend the standard scramble back to camp, strike the tent and hike out, or spend a second night and walk out fresh. A car-to-car day is possible for a strong, fast party but leaves no margin: it is about 13 trail-and-scramble miles with roughly 3,900 ft of gain plus four pitches of 5.10.
wa_mount_blum_north_ridge: Typically a 2-day trip: Day 1 approach to a Blum Lakes-area camp; Day 2 glacier crossing and the ridge itself (~6 hours climbing time reported), then descent — one recent ascent logged about 20 hours car-to-car across 2 days.
wa_mount_constance_north_chute: Day 1: approach to Lake Constance. Day 2: pre-dawn ascent of Avalanche Canyon and the North Chute, cross the Finger Traverse, summit, descend. Day 3: hike out.
wa_mount_despair_northeast_buttress: A three-day outing: one long, arduous day of brush approach into the Goodell Creek valley and up to the base of the buttress, one full day climbing the buttress to the north summit, and an exit day out via Triumph Pass and Thornton Lakes Trail.
wa_mount_fury_east_direct_east_ridge: Day 1: Ross Dam trailhead, water taxi to Big Beaver Landing, then 11-12 miles of trail past Luna Camp, the Big Beaver log crossing and the Access Creek bushwhack to camp in Access Creek Basin at 4,300 ft (9+ hours from the landing is typical). Day 2: scree chute to Access Col at 6,100 ft and the steep heather traverse to Luna Col at about 7,200 ft (4-5 hours), set up high camp; Luna Peak, the finest viewpoint in Washington, is an easy Class 2-3 bonus summit that afternoon. Day 3: alpine start, traverse to the 6,300 ft basin, climb the Direct East Ridge to the summit and return to Luna Col - a full 12-15 hour day. Day 4: break camp, traverse back over Access Col, drop into Access Basin, reverse the bushwhack and hike the Big Beaver trail to a pre-booked evening water taxi (10-17 hours). Strong parties compress this to three days; most take four.
wa_mount_fury_east_north_buttress: Day 1: Ross Dam TH, water taxi, Big Beaver Trail and the Access Creek bushwhack to Access Creek Basin at 4,300 ft. Day 2: Access Col at 6,100 ft and the heather traverse to Luna Col at about 7,200 ft. Day 3: descend about 2,400 ft into Luna Cirque, past Luna Lake at 4,800 ft, and establish a cirque camp at the foot of the buttress. Day 4: pre-dawn start, climb the North Buttress - about 4.5 hours of climbing gets you to the ridge crest, with the 5.9 crux and the summit snow arete above - then descend the Southeast Glacier and the northeast ridge to Luna Col, or bivouac high. Day 5: exit Luna Col to Access Basin, reverse the bushwhack, Big Beaver Trail to a booked water taxi. Five days is realistic; six gives you a weather day, which on a north-facing 4,000-ft line in the Pickets you will probably want. Kearney's September attempt stretched from a planned 7 days to 10 when a storm dumped heavy snow.
wa_mount_howard_south_slope: Commonly done car-to-car in a single long day (about 7.5-8.75 hours round trip reported from Merritt Lake TH for Howard alone or Howard+Mastiff combined). A 2-day version is also used, especially for spring snow climbs or when combining multiple Nason Ridge summits: Day 1 — trailhead to a bivy near Crescent Lake or the summit (about 12 miles, 6,000-6,400 ft gain); Day 2 — summit (if not reached Day 1) and return to the trailhead.
wa_mount_index_north_face: Common plan: Day 1 — hike in to Lake Serene (or bivy at the lake/talus basin below the route); Day 2 — pre-dawn start, climb the North Face (roughly a full day with the approach), and descend/rappel back to the lake, hiking out that evening. Strong parties occasionally do it car-to-car in one very long day.
wa_mount_lago_south_slope_south_face: A common 3-day plan: Day 1 - hike in from the Robinson Creek or Slate Pass trailhead to Fred's Lake or Shellrock Basin. Day 2 - climb Mount Lago (often combined with Mount Carru via the connecting saddle) from a Shellrock Basin camp, roughly a half-day round trip. Day 3 - hike out. Many parties extend to 4-5 days to add Osceola Peak, Mount Rolo, or a full Pasayten ridge traverse (e.g. via Ptarmigan Peak and Dot Mountain).
wa_mount_maude_r2: Day 1: Approach ~4,000 ft of gain over several hours from the trailhead to a bivy site above Ice Lakes. Day 2: Descend to and cross the Entiat Glacier, climb the icefall (running belay through ice steps) then ~900 ft of 4th/low-5th class rock to the summit, descend the South Ridge back toward camp. Day 3: Hike out.
wa_mount_maude_r3: Day 1: Hike ~5 mi / ~2,700 ft from the Phelps Creek Trailhead to a camp in Leroy Creek Basin. Day 2: Approach the west side of the peak, climb the Nothing Couloir (class 3-4 slabs, ~1,500 ft) to the summit ridge and summit, then descend via the South Shoulder in a loop back to camp. Day 3: Hike out.
wa_mount_noyes_standard: Multi-day backpack with a high camp near Low Divide, reached via the North Fork Quinault River Trail (~16 mi), or the much longer Elwha River Trail from Whiskey Bend (~28 mi, lengthened by the Olympic Hot Springs Road washout, which has closed the road to vehicles beyond Madison Falls since November 2017).
wa_mount_pershing_standard: Long day trip (~8 miles round trip, 10–11 hours) from the Jefferson Creek trailhead off FR 2401 in the Hamma Hamma drainage; a basin camp is an option for a more relaxed overnight pace.
wa_mount_persis_west_ridge: Single-day, car-to-car outing: drive FR-62 to the road-end trailhead (allow extra time/mileage if the highway gate is locked), climb the West Ridge boot path to the summit (roughly 2-3 hours of climbing), enjoy summit views, then descend the same way. Total car-to-car time is commonly reported as 4.5+ hours given the steepness and route-finding, longer in winter conditions or if the road gate forces an extended approach.
wa_mount_pilchuck_east_ridge: Single day: drive to the Pinnacle Lake Trailhead, hike to Pinnacle Lake, scramble via Iodine Gulch to Bathtub Lakes (optional turnaround point), then continue to the summit and return the same way — a longer, more committing full-day outing than the standard trail.
wa_mount_pilchuck_standard_route: Single-day round trip: drive to the FR 42 trailhead, hike up via Trail #700, spend time at the lookout, then descend the same trail — a full day out once drive time from the Seattle/Everett area is included.
wa_mount_price_hester_lake_route: Full, often long day: Dingford Creek TH -> ~5-6 mi trail to the Hester Lake basin -> off-trail gully/boulder-field/ridge scramble to the summit -> reverse descent. At least one trip report logged roughly 10.5 hours car-to-car; start early and carry a headlamp.
wa_mount_prophet_east: Typically a 2-3 day trip: hike or water-taxi in to the Thirtynine Mile Creek area, high camp at the saddle on the south ridge crest, summit day via the ridge, then exit back down Big Beaver Trail.
wa_mount_prophet_southwest_rib: Typically a 2-3 day trip: hike/boat in to Luna Camp on Day 1, climb the rib to the summit and return to camp on Day 2 (or continue over the South/Southeast Ridge as a loop), hike/boat out on Day 3.
wa_mount_pugh_pika_slab: Day trip. This is a single very long day: leave the trailhead at first light, reach Lake Metan in about 45-60 minutes, Stujack Pass in roughly 2.5-3 hours, and the Pika Slab crag band about 30-45 minutes above the pass. Climb the slab (a matter of minutes), continue to the summit for the view if weather allows, then reverse everything, allowing 2-3 hours down. Budget 7-9 hours car to car and be honest that the 5,300 ft of gain on the full peak day is among the largest of any Washington trail that reaches a true summit. If you want a shorter summit day there are a few camp spots at the base of Stujack Pass, but water above Lake Metan is unreliable, so you must carry it up.
wa_mount_rahm_custer_traverse: Typically day 2 or 3 of a Depot Creek (Ouzel Lake) or Silver Creek approach trip: climb one peak via its standard line, make the traverse (about an hour), then descend the other peak's own route back to camp.
wa_mount_rahm_south_side: Day 1: hike in to Ouzel Lake (via Depot Creek, including a border crossing) or Silver Lake (via the Silver Creek bushwhack) and camp. Day 2: climb the South Side route to Rahm's summit (about 2 hrs from Silver Lake or 3-5 hrs from Ouzel Lake) and return to camp, or continue to Custer/Spickard. Day 3: hike out.
wa_mount_rainier_edmunds_headwall: 3-4 days: approach from Mowich to a base camp, climb the headwall in a summit day to Liberty Cap, then descend a standard route.
wa_mount_rainier_fuhrer_thumb: Done in 1-2 days similar to the Finger, with an early start to climb the couloir cold.
wa_mount_sefrit_southeast_ridge: Single-push day: drive to the Ruth Creek Road pullout near milepost 3 (2,950 ft); cross Ruth Creek and bushwhack to the base of Wall Street (~45 min); climb the snow couloir to the Northwest Glacier (~5,000 ft); cross the glacier to the 6,500-ft saddle; scramble the southeast ridge to the 7,191-ft summit (about 5.6 hours car-to-summit for one party); descend the same line (about 2.8 hours back to the car).
wa_mount_spickard_silver_glacier: Day 1: water-taxi and hike (or Depot Creek hike) in to camp at Silver Lake or Ouzel Lake.
