Day 2: from Ouzel Lake climb the gully to the Custer-Spickard saddle (from Silver Lake, cross the moraine to the glacier toe), cross the Silver Glacier, and climb the summit step (roughly 3-4 hours summit-bound from Silver Lake camp), then return to camp. Day 3: hike/water-taxi out.
wa_mount_teneriffe_kamikaze_trail: Typical day trip: start early morning; ~1-1.5 hrs to the Teneriffe Falls/Kamikaze junction (2.8 mi); ~2-2.5 hrs of steep boot-track climbing to the ridge crest and summit (~4.1 mi, about +4,000 ft); short summit break; descend either back down Kamikaze (~2.5 hrs) or via the standard trail loop (~3-3.5 hrs).
wa_mount_teneriffe_standard_route: Typical day trip: start early morning; ~1.5-2 hrs for the first 2.8 mi; ~2.5-3 hrs more via the upper switchbacks and Rachor Pass to the summit (6.5 mi, +3,800 ft); 30-45 min on the summit; ~3 hrs back down the same trail. Budget 7-9 hours car-to-car.
wa_mount_terror_stoddard_buttress: Day 1: hike to the high camp in Crescent Creek Basin. Day 2: alpine start, cross the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col and Mustard Glacier to the route base, climb the buttress crest and knife-edge finish to the summit, descend via the West Ridge notch and gully rappels (a long day, ~17 hrs camp-to-camp for one party). Day 3: hike out.
wa_mount_terror_west_ridge: Day 1: approach to Crescent Creek Basin (~6,000 ft gain). Day 2: climb the gully to the West Ridge notch, complete the short technical section and summit scramble, then descend the same way. Day 3: hike out.
wa_mount_triumph_northeast_ridge: Standard plan is 3 days: Day 1 — drive in and hike to the bivy col above Thornton Lakes (~5 hrs); Day 2 — climb the Northeast Ridge round-trip from the col (roughly 6 hrs up, 6 hrs down, a 12-13+ hour day) and sleep again at the col; Day 3 — hike out. Strong parties occasionally push it as a long 2-day trip with one bivy, but the extra day is usually recommended given the length and complexity.
wa_mount_washington_olympic_winter_direc: Single winter/spring day: approach from Jefferson Pass through drainages, the single technical pitch near the summit, then the long roped-descent down snow slopes.
wa_narcos: Single-day car-to-car outing: early start, 1-1.5 hr unmarked approach, climb (allow several hours for 5 pitches with route-finding on an obscure line), 4 raps to descend, reverse the approach.
wa_ne_couloir: Single day, ideally with an early (pre-dawn or early-morning) start to catch firm snow: drive to Tiffany Springs Campground, hike ~45 min to Honeymoon Pass, traverse to the cirque, climb the couloir, then walk off via the NW ridge and Little Tiffany Lake trail — roughly 5 hours round-trip.
wa_ne_ridge: Day 1: drive to trailhead, hike toward Cathedral Pass, camp. Day 2: continue to Upper Cathedral Lake basin. Day 3: climb the ridge, descend to camp. Days 4-5: hike out.
wa_needle_peak_north_ridge: Day 1: hike from Stehekin via the Agnes Creek Trail to Swamp Creek, climb Needle Peak's North Ridge, continue over the North and South Anonymity Towers, climb the Dark Glacier, and bivouac atop Dark Peak. Day 2: continue the connecting ridge crest to Bonanza Peak's west summit and then the main summit, descending via the Mary Greene Glacier.
wa_nooksack_tower_south_face: Typically run from a high camp: approach across the East Nooksack Glacier to the base of the face, climb the 12-pitch route to the summit, then descend via the north face route back to the glacier and camp. The first ascensionists completed the entire round trip from their high camp in about 17 hours.
wa_north_face_left_buttress: From the lawful Ross Lake side the walk in to a camp below the north face is itself a multi-day trip, so plan on more than 3 days car to car. The Manning Park line, which is not a lawful border crossing, runs 3+ days: day 1 to a high camp near the border/Crow Creek basin, day 2 climb the route and descend to camp, day 3+ hike back out. The approach length makes this a serious multi-day undertaking rather than a single push.
wa_north_gardner_mountain_nw_couloir: Typically done as a long single day from the Cedar Creek Trailhead (one recorded ascent: 4h26m up, 2h40m down), though an overnight approach has also been used given the trail-less terrain and creek crossing.
wa_north_gardner_mountain_southwest: Typically done as an overnight or multi-day trip, with a high camp at Gardner Meadows (~10 miles in) or higher in Wolf Creek Basin (~6,200-6,400 ft) below the peak.
wa_north_ridge_7: Day 1: Drive Cascade River Road to the Boston Basin trailhead (~3,200 ft); hike ~3-4 mi / ~3,000 ft gain to high camp (~6,400 ft). Day 2: Early start from camp, climb to the col and up the North Ridge to the tower and back (a half-day round trip is typical); hike out or stay a second night.
wa_north_ridge_west_side: Day 1: Drive to Cutthroat Lake trailhead or Rainy Pass. Hike to approach base (3-4 hours via Cutthroat Lake route, or 2-3 hours via PCT). Scout route and camp if needed. Day 2: Climb North Ridge - West Side (6-8 hours total from base for approach, climb, and descent). Conclude descent by mid-afternoon to avoid scrambling in dark.
wa_north_tower_ridge_route: Single long day: drive to Tiffany Springs Campground, hike ~45 min to Honeymoon Pass, traverse ~30 min to the base of the climb, climb the 6-pitch route (a few hours for a competent party), then walk off via the NW ridge and Little Tiffany Lake trail back to the car.
wa_north_twin_sister_west_ridge: A long day: reports give roughly 6-7 hours from trailhead to summit and 4-5 hours back down, on top of the logging-road approach.
wa_northeast_face_direct: Day 1: Cascade Pass trailhead to Kool-Aid Lake via Cascade Pass, Mixup Arm, Cache Glacier and Cache Col (~5 hrs); camp. Day 2: pre-dawn start, cross the Middle Cascade Glacier basin to the face base, climb the Direct Northeast Face (roughly 8-10.5 hrs from camp to summit), then descend via the South Route back to camp. Day 3: hike out to the trailhead.
wa_northeast_ridge_1963_route: Typically climbed over 2 days: Day 1 — approach from the Cascade Pass trailhead to a high bivy near the base of the Northeast Face/C-J couloir; Day 2 — climb the route to the summit, then descend via the East Ridge/C-J col and Doug's Direct back to the car (a long day; some parties add a 3rd day).
wa_northwest_face_4: Day 1: Hike in from the Dingford Creek Trailhead (the closed road, then the trail to the steel bridge, plus additional cross-country travel) and establish camp at the ~4,650' gravel wash in Summit Chief Valley. Day 2: Climb the Northwest Face (Falcon Route) and descend via the south ridge/pocket glacier back to camp. Day 3: Hike out to the trailhead.
wa_olympus_summit_block_west_edge: Same as Blue Glacier standard route; variation only on summit block.
wa_one_piece_at_a_time: Full day: early start, approach to base (roughly 1-2 hrs from the trailhead), 6 pitches (4-6 hrs), then three rappels to descend (about 1-1.5 hrs).
wa_painted_traverse: Very fit, fast parties do it in a single long day starting before dawn; most parties take two to three days, camping near Black Mountain where water is most reliable.
wa_plan_9_from_outer_space: Typically done as part of a multi-day Southern Pickets trip: Day 1, backpack in via the Goodell Creek roadbed and Terror Creek climbers' path to a high camp near the Barrier or in Terror Basin; Day 2, cross the Barrier into Crescent Creek Basin and establish camp within striking distance of the Himmelhorn/Blob area; Day 3, climb Plan 9 from Outer Space and return to camp via the Blob/Terror col rappels; Day 4, hike out.
wa_playing_not_spraying: Day 1: Drive to the Cedar Creek Trailhead, hike ~5 miles up the Cedar Creek Trail, leave the trail below the old burn, and work up along the south-face drainage to camp in the meadows at ~6,200 ft. Day 2: Climb the 8-pitch route, rappel the SE side back to camp, and hike out via Cedar Creek Trail.
wa_poltergeist_pinnacle: Day 1: Drive to the Hannegan Pass Trailhead and hike roughly 16 mi via Hannegan Pass, the Chilliwack River ford, Easy Ridge, and the Imperfect Impasse to camp at Perfect Pass (a full day; ~7,000 ft of gain). Day 2: Rope up and cross the Challenger Glacier to the base of Poltergeist Pinnacle (roughly 3 hours from camp per the first-ascent account), climb the East Face route (3 technical pitches plus ~800 ft of simul-climbed ridge), traverse to Mount Challenger's summit, and descend the Challenger Glacier back to Perfect Pass camp. Day 3: Hike out to the trailhead.
wa_ptarmigan_traverse: Day 1 (Cascade Pass to Kool-Aid Lake): 4-6 hours, ~3,300 ft gain. Hike Cascade Pass Trail to the pass (3.7 miles), then off-trail south to Cache Col crossing on Cache Glacier, descend to Kool-Aid Lake bivouac (elevation ~6,100 ft). Day 2 (Kool-Aid to Yang-Yang Lakes): 8-11 hours, 2,500 ft gain/loss. Cross the exposed Red Ledge below Art's Knoll (Class 3 scrambling), climb the Middle Cascade Glacier to Spider-Formidable Col, descend to Yang-Yang Lakes bivouac. Day 3 (Yang-Yang to White Rock Lakes): 7-11 hours, 2,000 ft gain/loss. Traverse Le Conte Ridge, cross Le Conte Glacier with crevasse hazards, descend to White Rock Lakes bivouac (visual highlight of entire route). Day 4 (White Rock rest day or peak day): Optional rest day. Dome Peak (8,924 ft) is climbed from the Itswoot Ridge camp instead, via the Dome Glacier route (35-degree snow and ice), as an extra day after Day 5. Day 5 (White Rock to Itswoot Ridge): 8-10 hours, 3,000 ft gain. Ascend Dana Glacier crossing bergschrund, summit Spire Point (8,264 ft) or traverse below on east face, descend to Itswoot Ridge bivouac. Day 6 (Itswoot to Downey Creek TH): 8-12 hours, 2,500 ft loss. Descend Bachelor Creek through forest, reach Downey Creek Trailhead. Alternative faster options: out-and-back from Cascade Pass (4-5 days), or extend to Dome Peak summit and add Sentinel Peak/Old Guard (7-8 days).
wa_ragged_ridge: Commonly done either as a long single day (~13-14 hrs car-to-car) from Easy Pass, or as a 2-day trip: Day 1 — approach via Easy Pass and Fisher Creek to a high camp (~6,700 ft) on Mesahchie's south shoulder; Day 2 — traverse Mesahchie-Katsuk-Kimtah-Cosho and descend to the Fisher Creek trail.
wa_rampage: Most parties climb Rampage alone as a long single day car-to-car, or link it with a Burgundy Spire route (e.g. Action Potential) for a bigger day; one documented Burgundy linkup ran roughly 6 AM to just before 7 PM (~13 hrs) for 12 combined pitches.
wa_raven_ridge_southeast_ridge_crater_la: The documented winter ascent (Gilbertson & Robinson, Jan 2019) skied in from an unplowed road to camp at Crater Lake, summited and returned to camp the same day, then skied/hiked out the next day. A summer visit via the maintained Crater Creek/Crater Lakes Trail (7.8 miles round trip to the lake) could reasonably be done as a single long day or a lighter two-day trip with a camp at the lake.
wa_raven_ridge_standard_route: Most parties climb Raven Ridge as a single long day from the Libby Lake Trailhead (roughly 12–13 miles round trip with about 4,200 ft of gain). Parties combining Raven Ridge with Hoodoo Peak often backpack in about 5 miles to camp near the old cabin (~7,170 ft) or at Libby Lake, climb both peaks via the connecting ridge on day two, and hike out on day three (or as a very long single day for fit, fast parties).
wa_remmel_mountain_nw_ridge: Day 1: Bushwhack from Remmel Lake south through forests and bogs to reach camp at 7,500 feet on lower ridge. Day 2: Climb from camp to summit (3.5 hours typical climbing time from camp), summit and rappel descent back to camp (2.5 hours), return to Remmel Lake.
wa_remmel_mountain_southeast_slope: Typically a 2-3 day backpack: Day 1 hike in to camp at Four Point Lake or along the Chewuch/Andrews Creek Trail; Day 2 climb to the summit and return to camp; Day 3 hike out. Strong parties have also completed the whole round trip (25+ miles, 5,500-6,800 ft gain) as a single very long day.
wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury: Day 1: Water taxi from Ross Dam to Big Beaver, hike 9.4 miles to Luna Camp. Day 2: Climb Access Creek and Access Col to a high camp at Luna Col. Day 3: From Luna Col, ascend East Fury, traverse to West Fury, and return over East Fury to Luna Col. Day 4: Descend Access Creek and the Big Beaver Trail to Ross Lake for the water taxi return.
wa_roan_wall_center_stage: Feasible in a single long day (~3-3.5 hr approach, full 10-pitch climb, rappel descent, ~3-3.5 hr exit), or split by bivying at the Martha's Place boulder near the base the night before to shorten the climbing day. Pairs with Flight of the Falcon on Salish Peak for a big linkup for fast, motivated parties.
wa_roan_wall_stage_right: Typically a long single day given the shared ~3-3.5 hr approach with Center Stage, full 10-pitch climb, and rappel descent via Center Stage's anchors; alternatively bivy at Martha's Place near the base the night before to shorten the summit day.
wa_robinson_mountain_southeast_ridge: Commonly done as a very long single day (~14-15 miles round trip, ~6,100-6,500 ft gain, reported car-to-car times around 12 hours) or as an overnight, camping at the Southeast Robinson Tarn (or lower in Beauty Creek valley or at the Robinson Creek bridge) to split the approach and summit push into two days.
wa_rock_mountain_northeast_ridge: Typically a 2-day, roughly 15-mile traverse: Day 1 - Old Merritt Lake TH to Merritt Lake, over Mt. Mastiff and Mt. Howard to a camp at Upper Canaan Lake Basin (~6,050 ft; ~6,000 ft of cumulative gain to that point). Day 2 - cross the Howard-Rock col, climb Rock Mountain's northeast side, then descend the South Ridge-East Slope past Rock Lake and out the Rock Mountain Trail to the US-2 trailhead (roughly 6,300 ft of cumulative loss over the full traverse). These distance/elevation figures describe the entire 3-peak traverse, not an isolated Rock Mountain ascent.
wa_ruby_mountain_south_ridge: Day 1: Trailhead to Fourth of July Camp (4.8 mi, ~2,300 ft gain, ~2.7 hrs), set up camp (permanent water source at camp, but none higher on the mountain by mid-summer). Day 2: Camp to summit (~4,000 ft gain, ~6.1 hrs), summit to camp (~3.6 hrs), camp to trailhead (~1.7 hrs). Strong parties can also do it as a single very long day.
wa_scramble_route: Typically a single long day trip from Longmire: trailhead to the Eagle Peak-Chutla saddle (~3.6 mi one-way, ~2,900 ft gain), saddle to summit via the ridge scramble (short distance, roughly 250-300 ft of additional gain over uneven terrain), then reverse the full route to the trailhead — on the order of 7-9 miles and ~3,200 ft round trip depending on the exact line taken through the summit scramble.
wa_se_ridge_aka_shield_wall: Long single day: approach roughly 1-1.25 hrs from the trailhead to the base of the wall, climb 7 pitches (low 5th-5.7) up the Shield Wall, make up to three 30m rappels through the ridge's gendarmes, climb about 6 more pitches (3rd-5.7) to the summit, then descend via the standard route back to the car.
wa_sherpa_balanced_rock_ne_couloir: Approach from the Stuart Lake Trailhead to a camp in the basin between Sherpa and Argonaut below the couloir; alpine-start to climb the couloir (snow/ice to roughly 50 degrees) to its top, then scramble up and right to the Balanced Rock summit via a short 5.0 pitch; descend the same route or via Sherpa Pass.
wa_sinister_peak_north_face: Follows the same 2-3 day approach to a high camp near Itswoot Ridge/Dome Glacier as the Southwest Route. From high camp, cross to the Dome-Chickamin col, descend onto the Chickamin Glacier, climb the north face directly to the summit, then return to camp and reverse the approach over 1-2 more days.
wa_slippery_slab_tower_ne_face: Day 1 (if overnight): Depart early morning from Tunnel Creek Trailhead, reach Hope Lake (2-2.5 hrs), continue over Trap Pass and camp at Trap Lake just below it (2-3 additional hours of approach). Day 2: Climb Slippery Slab Tower and return to camp (6-8 hrs). Day 3: Return to trailhead (4-5 hrs). For day trip, depart before dawn and allow 10-12 hours total.
wa_south_face: Commonly done car-to-car in one long day (approach roughly 3-4 hours each way, plus a few hours on route and descent), or split over two days with a bivy at 'The Ledge' (~2 miles in) or at Burgundy Col itself (~7,800 ft) — a good base if linking Vasiliki with Burgundy Spire or other nearby Wine Spires towers.
wa_south_face_10: Day 1: drive to trailhead and hike in toward Upper Cathedral Lake basin; Day 2: continue to basecamp if needed and rest/scout; Day 3: climb the South Face car-to-car from camp; Day 4: hike out.
wa_south_gully_south_spur: A half day in good conditions and most of a day in bad ones. From the Summit West lot in firm winter snow, about an hour of approach up Commonwealth to the base of the gully, then three rope lengths to the first chockstone, a second chockstone and the short ice or rock step above it, and out onto the South Spur to the south summit. If you want the true traverse, continue over the middle summit, make the rappel, and finish up the north summit. Descend west to Alpental or east down Commonwealth. One party in poor conditions - fog to 20 ft visibility, verglas, fresh snow - took most of a day and noted that in good conditions this is a great half-day outing, which is the honest range.
wa_south_rib: A half day to a full day, car to car, and a genuinely realistic after-work or short-weather-window objective given the drive from Seattle is under an hour. Park on Alpental Road, walk the ski track and boulder field to the base, and climb five pitches or simulclimb the easier ground. One fit party moving fast on a steep variation of this side of the peak reached the true south summit an hour and a half after leaving the car, which is the low end; a roped party of two on the standard rib should plan on the better part of a day. Descend north over the subsummits and out via the Southeast Couloir and the Cave Ridge trail. No camping needed or wanted.
wa_south_ridge: Multi-day trip from Stehekin (ferry up Lake Chelan, shuttle to High Bridge) or from Downey Creek in the west; plan 1-2 days of approach, a climbing day, and 1-2 days out.
wa_south_ridge_4: Day 1: approach to Eldorado high camp (~7,600 ft) via Eldorado Creek and Eldorado Glacier, 5-6 hrs. Day 2: climb the South Ridge (4 pitches) and descend the East Ridge. Day 3: hike out.
wa_south_ridge_6: Day 1: Drive to the Boston Basin trailhead and hike in to high camp (~6,400 ft). Day 2: Early start, approach via snowfields to the base of the South Ridge, climb the 5 pitches to the top, then descend via the North Ridge back to camp.
wa_southeast_ridge_se_corner: Typically a 2-3 day trip: Day 1 approach to a bivy near Winnie's Slide or the Sulphide high camp; Day 2 alpine start, cross the glaciers to the Pyramid notch, climb the SE Ridge to the summit, rappel back to the notch; Day 3 (or same day) descend to the trailhead.
wa_southwest_rib_2: Day 1: Drive to Ingalls Creek Trailhead and backpack in via the Ingalls Creek Trail and the Crystal Creek/Nightmare Gorge boot path to a camp in Crystal Creek Basin or at Crystal Lake. Day 2: Climb the Southwest Rib (roughly 19 pitches) to the summit, then descend via the Westernmost Chessman to the Enchantment Plateau or back to Crystal Lake; return to camp. Day 3: Hike out via Crystal Creek and Ingalls Creek Trail to the trailhead.
wa_sperry_peak_east_face: A long day or overnight: the FA party needed 7-8 hours on the route alone and bivied at the summit after arriving in the dark.
wa_sperry_peak_upper_south_ridge: Reckon on most of a day - plan for a full day out given the approach to Headlee Pass plus 8 pitches/sections of low-5th climbing and scrambling.
wa_spider_mountain_north_ridge: Day 1: Drive to Cascade Pass Trailhead; hike via Cascade Pass and Cache Col to a base camp at Kool-Aid Lake or Spider-Formidable Col (roughly 6-8 miles). Day 2: Climb Spider Mountain via the southeast gully/east ridge (about 3 hours col-to-summit, roughly 8 hours car-to-car equivalent from Kool-Aid Lake); many parties combine it with Mount Formidable from the same camp. Day 3: Hike out to the trailhead.
wa_spontaneity_arete: Pre-dawn/early start from the car; ~1-1.5 hr approach to the base; roughly 4-6 hours for the 6-7 pitches including route-finding and scrambling between belays; 2-3+ hours for the rappel/gully descent back to the creek crossing and pullout — full car-to-car days of 9+ hours are commonly reported.
wa_spontaneous_distraction: Roughly 1.5 hours approach, a few hours for the 4 pitches, and a comparatively quick single-rope rappel descent — a shorter day overall than the neighboring Spontaneity Arête.
wa_star_peak_sawtooth_nw_ridge: Backpack in via the same trail to a camp at Star Lake or near Fish Creek Pass, then climb the ridge as a technical day trip from camp; allow a full day given the approach length and the ridge's sustained, low-angle length before the crux.
wa_summertime: Single day from Mazama: ~20-25 min approach, climb 5 pitches (Grade II, ~400 ft) of mixed bolts and trad gear to the clifftop, then rappel the route back to the base.
wa_summit_chief_mountain_north_face: Day 1: Drive/bike the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road, hike/ford into the valley and establish camp below the north face (~6.5 hrs). Day 2: Alpine start (~6 AM), climb the ~2,000 ft ice line, descend the SW-side gully with two rappels, and hike back out.
wa_sw_couloir_and_face: Typically climbed as a long single push or with a bivy near Lake Ann/Lower Curtis Glacier.
wa_sw_ridge: Typically climbed as one route within a multi-day trip that also includes objectives on the neighboring South or North Gunsight towers: Day 1 - ferry/shuttle/hike to a streamside camp; Day 2 - approach to high camp below the glacier; Day 3 - climb the SW Ridge (often paired with another route the same trip); Day 4 - descend and hike out.
wa_swiss_peak_standard_route: Representative Northern Pickets crest plan: Day 1 — Ross Dam TH, water taxi across Ross Lake, Big Beaver Trail to Luna Camp/Access Creek. Day 2 — climb Access Creek drainage to the Luna Cirque basin, gain Luna Col, camp near Luna Col or continue toward East/West Fury. Day 3 — traverse East Fury, West Fury, cross the glacier/snowfield to the Swiss-Fury saddle, climb Swiss Peak's southwest face, continue toward Spectre Plateau. Day 4-5 — continue over Phantom Peak, Crooked Thumb, to Mt. Challenger and Whatcom Pass, exiting via Chilliwack River or Little Beaver trails. (A southern variant instead approaches via Bacon Creek/Porkbelly/Mystery Ridge over 4-5 days to Pickell Pass, climbs Swiss's south side in a 2.5-hour round trip from camp, then continues north over Challenger toward Whatcom Pass and out via Hannegan Pass.)
wa_tenpeak_mountain_north_couloir: Typically climbed as a long day from a high glacier camp (e.g. Kololo Peaks) or as part of a multi-day Glacier Peak-area traverse; a start before 6am is common to catch firm snow, with the couloir climbed in a few hours and the summit reached by mid-morning.
wa_the_brothers_traverse: Recommended overnight push: Day 1 - Hike from trailhead to climbers camp (6-7 hours, establish bivy). Day 2 - Traverse ridge, summit both peaks, return to camp (10-12 hours), or retreat to trailhead same day (add 4-5 hours). Alternatively, 2-day push from trailhead with overnight at higher camp.
wa_the_chalice: Day 1: Drive to Cedar Creek Trailhead and hike/approach to camp in the meadows near 6,200 ft below Silver Horn's south face. Day 2: Climb the 8-pitch route to the summit and descend, then hike back out via Cedar Creek Trail.
wa_the_monk_le_gibet: Day 1: hike 17–20 miles to Upper Cathedral Lake. Day 2: The Monk routes as a half day, then rest. Day 3: the Southeast Buttress or South Face on Cathedral proper. Day 4: hike out.
wa_the_monk_odine: Day 1: hike 17–20 miles to Upper Cathedral Lake. Day 2: Odine and another Monk route as a half day. Day 3: the Southeast Buttress. Day 4: hike out.
wa_the_monk_scabo: Day 1: hike 17–20 miles to Upper Cathedral Lake. Day 2: Scabo and a second Monk route as a half day. Day 3: the Southeast Buttress or South Face. Day 4: hike out.
wa_the_monk_west_cracks_left_crack: Best used as a filler: an afternoon pitch on your arrival day at Upper Cathedral Lake, or a short outing on a day when weather rules out the main wall. Otherwise it fits into a half-day on The Monk alongside Odine or Scabo.
wa_the_monk_west_cracks_right_crack: A filler objective: an arrival-afternoon route, an easy day when the main wall is wet, or the warm-up half of a Monk day with Odine or Scabo.
wa_the_perfect_crime_with_variations: Full day: early start, roughly 1-2 hr approach to base, 4-6 hrs for the route (more if exploring optional variations), then about 1-1.5 hrs to descend.
wa_the_tiger: A full day from the car: 40–60 minute approach, 11 pitches (commonly 8–10+ hours for a competent party), then a multi-rappel descent of roughly 1.5–3 hours — plan for a long car-to-car day.
wa_the_tipping_point: Day push (the common choice, and no overnight permit is needed): leave the Stuart Lake Trailhead before first light, be at Colchuck Lake around sunrise, at the base of the wall by mid-morning after 3-4 hours of approach, climbing by late morning. The west face is in shade all morning and gets sun in the afternoon, which is a real asset on a cold day and a liability on a hot one. Allow 8 hours or more on the route — the crux pitches reward working the sequences rather than rushing — 1 hour for the descent to the base, and 3 hours to hike out. Realistic car-to-car is 14 to 17 hours. Two-day version: win or walk up an Enchantment Permit Area overnight permit for the Colchuck zone, hike in on day one to a bivy near the lake or on the boulders in the west basin, climb rested on day two, and hike out that evening. That turns the crux pitches from a stopwatch problem into a climbing problem, and it is the version most parties who send the route describe.
wa_the_tooth_fairy: Trailhead start pre-dawn to mid-morning -> ~1.5-2 hr approach to the basin below the west face -> rack up and climb 6 pitches (allow 3-5 hours depending on party size and traffic) -> short scramble to the true summit -> rappel the route or the South Face -> retrace the approach to the trailhead.
wa_the_tooth_indentured_servant: Single-day car-to-car climb sharing the South Face/Tooth Fairy approach; a full day given the approach, 5 pitches, summit scramble, and descent.
wa_the_triad_traverse: Usually combined with an Eldorado Peak ascent and/or a longer Boston Basin circuit rather than climbed in isolation; budget a full day for the Triad ridge portion alone (11+ hours reported for a single-day East Ridge variant) or plan it as day one of a 2–4 day link-up with an appropriate car shuttle.
wa_three_queens_middle_peak: Single long day: trailhead to summit via South Face/South Chimney (documented ascent time ~4.9 hrs), summit to trailhead (~3.6 hrs descent), for roughly 10 miles round trip and 4,600 ft of gain/loss.
wa_three_queens_west_peak: 2-day trip documented: Day 1, trailhead to Spectacle Point camp via Kachess River, Mineral Creek, and Park Lakes; Day 2, West Ridge-West Face to the summit and return to the trailhead (16 miles, 5,300 ft gain/loss total in the accounts report).
wa_tooth_chair_traverse: Early trailhead start -> approach to base of a chosen Tooth route (South Face is typical) -> climb to The Tooth's summit -> traverse the ridge crest toward Chair Peak (3-4 hours of ridge climbing, including one rappel off Bryant Peak and a short forested walking section) -> climb to Chair Peak's summit -> descend Chair Peak's standard gully -> hike out, for a full day requiring good fitness and comfort on sustained exposed terrain.
wa_tower_arete: Single day: drive to Tiffany Springs Campground, hike ~45 min to Honeymoon Pass, ~30 min traverse to the arête base, climb the 5 sections (a shorter outing than the North Tower Ridge Route given the easier grade), then walk off via the NW ridge and Little Tiffany Lake trail.
wa_traverse_of_mount_index: Day 1: Hike to Lake Serene (2.5-3 hours). Begin climbing North Face section (6-7 hours to North Peak summit). Camp or bivy on North Peak. Day 2: Traverse to Middle Peak (1-2 hours), continue to Main Peak (1-2 hours). Descend via rappels to Lake Serene (2-3 hours). Exit to trailhead (1 hour).
wa_tupshin_peak_east_face: Day 1: Ferry/floatplane to Stehekin, hike Company Creek Trail (~3 mi) to the leave-trail point. Day 2: Traverse White Goat Mountain's west slopes and cross the ~7,200 ft pass above Bird Lakes to a high bivy in the Bird Lakes basin. Day 3: Climb the East Face (class 2-4 with a 5.4-5.6 crux) to the summit and return to camp. Day 4: Hike out to Stehekin.
wa_vanishing_point: Typically climbed as a 2-3 day trip mirroring the original ascent style: Day 1 — hike in and complete the ~3-3.5 hour technical approach (forested rib with fixed lines, roped slab) to the bivy caves below the tower; Day 2 — climb the full 14-pitch route (a very long day given sustained 5.10-5.12 climbing with few easy pitches); Day 3 (or same-day if fast) — descend via the ~3-hour descent route back to the trailhead. Strong parties also do the route car-to-car in one very long day (roughly 3 hours of approach, a full day on route, and about 3 hours of descent) with a pre-dawn start.
wa_washington_ellinor_traverse_ridge: From the Washington trailhead, climb the standard route to Washington's summit (~1.5 hrs at a moderate pace), then traverse the ridge to Ellinor's summit (one GPS-tracked report logged about 4.25 hrs total, trailhead-to-Ellinor-summit, over roughly 6 miles and 4,250 ft of cumulative gain), then descend Ellinor's trail and walk/shuttle back to a car.
wa_waterfall_buttress: Feasible as a long single day from the Squire Creek Road trailhead (~3-3.5 hr approach each way plus climbing and rappel descent), or shorten the summit day by hiking in the evening before and bivying at Martha's Place, which sits directly at the base of the buttress approach.
wa_west_craggy_peak_standard_route: Day 1: Drive to the Copper Glance Trailhead and hike ~3.3-3.5 miles with ~2,800 ft gain to a camp in Copper Glance Basin (~6,260-6,600 ft). Day 2: From camp, climb ~1,800 ft up talus/scree and the south gully to the south ridge and the summit (roughly 2.5-3 hours one-way), then descend to camp, break camp, and hike out. Strong parties often combine this with Big Craggy Peak and/or do the whole outing car-to-car in one long day.
wa_west_face_2: Day 1: Hike the Downey Creek Trail and the brushy Bachelor Creek path to camp at Bachelor Flats (about 4,500 ft), or push on to Cub Lake (long day with significant brush and blowdown on Bachelor Creek). Day 2: Over the pass to Cub Lake, up Itswoot Ridge and across the Dome Glacier to a high camp at the Dome-Chickamin col (about 8,500 ft). Day 3: Cross the Chickamin Glacier to the base of the West Face, climb the route (5-6 pitches), rappel, and return to the col. Days 4-5: Hike out over Itswoot Ridge and Cub Lake and down the Bachelor Creek and Downey Creek trails. Carry a spare day for weather.
wa_west_ridge_2: Commonly climbed car-to-car in a single long day (roughly 10-13 hours total). Many parties instead camp overnight at the ~6,500 ft bench and combine the route with a climb of the Silver Star glacier and/or Burgundy Spire's North Face on the same trip.
wa_windy_peak_windy_creek_trail: Doable as a single long day given the shorter mileage; can also be paired with a Cathedral Lakes/Cathedral Peak visit from the same general trailhead area for a multi-day trip.
wa_wing_peak_northwest_ridge: Commonly done as a 2-3 day trip: Day 1, hike/bushwhack from the Barclay Lake Trailhead to camp near Tailgunner Pass (~3,200-3,400 ft gain, roughly 6-7 hrs); Day 2 (optional), tag Gunn Peak and/or Tailgunner Peak from camp; final day, climb Wing Peak's northwest ridge from camp (~2.5 hrs up), then descend all the way to the trailhead (~4 hrs).
wa_winter_spring_ice_snow_mixed_2_east_f: A single long winter/spring day: early approach from Alpental through the Source Lake basin to the base of the East Face, 5 pitches of mixed/ice/snow climbing, then rappelling the South Face and returning via the same basin approach.
wa_witches_tower_southwest_corner: Can be done in one day, but parties often recommend two days combined with Dragontail Peak, camping at the col or near Aasgard Pass.
wa_witches_tower_west_buttress: Documented as a long single day (14 mi round trip, 5,400 ft gain, dawn-to-dark car-to-car) but could be broken into an overnight with a permit and camp near Colchuck Lake or Aasgard Pass.
wa_wright_pond: Single-day car-to-car climb: early start, 1-1.5 hr off-trail approach, 4 pitches to III 5.11 (allow several hours given sustained, technical, and runout climbing), 4 raps to descend, reverse the approach.
